definition: An empirical solar-radiation estimation model attributed to Abdallah that relates solar radiation to routinely measured meteorological variables.
comment: It is calibrated with station data and compared with other empirical correlations to estimate solar radiation at sites such as Ahvaz where pyranometer data are scarce.

definition: An empirical solar-radiation model that estimates global, direct and diffuse hourly irradiance from meteorological inputs using adaptively fitted coefficients.
comment: It relates hourly irradiance components to routinely measured meteorological variables through locally adapted coefficients; it is used to estimate solar irradiance where radiometric measurements are missing.
empiricalModelParameters: \alpha: adaptive ratio/model factor; P_s,V,S_P,R_d,T_B,V_l,r_0: variables/terms defined by the source model; b_i: fitted parameters

definition: A boosting ensemble method that builds a strong learner as a weighted combination of weak learners trained sequentially on reweighted samples.
comment: Each new weak learner (usually a shallow decision tree) gives more weight to samples poorly predicted by the previous ones, and the learners are combined by weighted voting or averaging. In renewable-energy studies it is used to predict solar radiation, wind speed or power output from meteorological inputs.

definition: An adaptive Kalman-filter nowcaster is a recursive state-space estimator with a time-varying system function used for very-short-term prediction.
comment: It recursively predicts and updates a hidden state from incoming measurements while adapting the system function over time; in solar and wind studies it is used to nowcast power or irradiance, here with a ramp-down correction.
timeSeriesModelFormula: x_t = F_t x_(t−1) + w_t ; y_t = H_t x_t + v_t, with w_t ~ N(0,Q_t) and v_t ~ N(0,R_t)
timeSeriesModelParameters: x_t: hidden state vector ; y_t: observation ; F_t: state-transition (system) matrix ; H_t: observation matrix ; Q_t: process-noise covariance ; R_t: measurement-noise covariance

definition: A neuro-fuzzy model that implements a Takagi–Sugeno fuzzy inference system whose membership-function and consequent parameters are learned with neural-network training.
comment: ANFIS tunes fuzzy if-then rules with hybrid least-squares and gradient-descent learning; it is widely used to predict solar radiation, wind speed and power output.

modelName: adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system - salp swarm algorithm - grasshopper optimization algorithm hybrid model
definition: A hybrid model in which an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system is trained or tuned by combined salp swarm and grasshopper optimization algorithms.
comment: The metaheuristics search the ANFIS membership-function and consequent parameters to minimise prediction error; it is used to forecast renewable-energy variables such as solar radiation or wind speed.

definition: The analytic hierarchy process is a multi-criteria decision-making method that derives criterion weights from pairwise comparisons organized in a hierarchy.
comment: Experts compare criteria pairwise on a ratio scale, weights are obtained from the principal eigenvector of the comparison matrix and checked with a consistency ratio; it is widely used to weight criteria in renewable-energy site suitability analyses.

modelName: analytic hierarchy process geographic information system concentrated solar power suitability model
definition: A multi-criteria site-suitability model that combines Analytic Hierarchy Process weighting with GIS overlay analysis to map land suitable for concentrated solar power plants.
comment: AHP pairwise comparisons derive weights for climatic, topographic and location criteria, which are combined as weighted raster layers in a GIS; it is used to identify and rank candidate CSP sites.

modelName: analytical photovoltaic irradiance model - Bayesian-regularized neural network hybrid model
definition: A hybrid analytical-machine-learning framework that couples an analytical photovoltaic irradiance model with a Bayesian-regularized neural network for module temperature approximation.
comment: The analytical model estimates irradiance on the PV array while the Bayesian-regularized network approximates temperature, with synthetic data generation and fractional-area MPPT, so that PV systems can be controlled without environmental sensors.

definition: An analytical wind-turbine capacity-factor model is a physical model that computes the expected output and capacity factor of a turbine by integrating its power curve over the wind-speed probability distribution.
comment: The turbine power curve is weighted by a fitted wind-speed density (typically Weibull) between cut-in and cut-out speeds to obtain mean power, which is divided by rated power; it is used to compare turbines and sites in wind resource assessment.
physicalModelFormula: CF = P_avg / P_r = (1/P_r) ∫ P(v) f(v) dv (integrated from cut-in speed v_ci to cut-out speed v_co)
physicalModelParameters: P(v): turbine power curve ; f(v): wind-speed probability density ; P_r: rated power ; v_ci: cut-in wind speed ; v_co: cut-out wind speed ; P_avg: mean output power
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: expected energy conversion of the wind kinetic energy flux by the turbine over the wind-speed distribution

definition: A hybrid model in which an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system is optimised by the differential evolution algorithm.
comment: Differential evolution searches the ANFIS parameters to reduce prediction error; it is applied to renewable-resource prediction tasks.

definition: A hybrid model in which an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system is optimised by a genetic algorithm.
comment: The genetic algorithm evolves the ANFIS premise and consequent parameters instead of or in addition to gradient-based training; it is applied to predict solar radiation, wind speed or power output.

definition: ANFIS-PSO is a hybrid model in which an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system is trained or tuned by particle swarm optimization.
comment: Particle swarm optimization searches the membership-function and consequent parameters of the ANFIS to reduce prediction error; it is used to forecast quantities such as solar radiation, wind speed or power output.

definition: An empirical linear model that estimates global solar radiation from relative sunshine duration.
comment: It relates the clearness index H/H0 linearly to the sunshine fraction S/S0 through locally calibrated coefficients; it is widely used to estimate global solar radiation at sites with sunshine records but no pyranometer data.
empiricalModelParameters: H: daily (or monthly mean daily) global solar radiation on a horizontal surface ; H0: extraterrestrial radiation on a horizontal surface ; S: measured sunshine duration ; S0: maximum possible sunshine duration (day length) ; a: regression constant ; b: regression coefficient
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Requires sunshine-duration records; coefficients a and b are site- and season-specific and must be calibrated locally

modelName: angular-linear inverse-Gaussian-lognormal distribution with 3 von Mises components
definition: An angular-linear joint distribution of wind speed and wind direction whose linear marginal is an inverse-Gaussian-lognormal mixture and whose angular parts are mixtures of three von Mises distributions.
comment: It follows the Johnson-Wehrly construction, linking the wind-speed and wind-direction marginals through a circular dependence density, and is used to describe the joint wind speed-direction regime for wind resource assessment.
distributionFormula: f(v,θ) = 2π g(ζ) f_V(v) f_Θ(θ), with ζ = 2π[F_V(v) − F_Θ(θ)]
distributionParameters: f_V, F_V: inverse-Gaussian-lognormal mixture pdf and cdf of wind speed ; f_Θ, F_Θ: pdf and cdf of a mixture of three von Mises distributions for wind direction ; g: von Mises mixture density of the circular variable ζ ; μ_j, κ_j, w_j: mean direction, concentration and weight of von Mises component j

modelName: angular-linear inverse-Gaussian-lognormal distribution with 6 von Mises components
definition: An angular-linear joint distribution of wind speed and direction whose linear marginal is an inverse-Gaussian–lognormal mixture and whose circular marginal is a mixture of six von Mises distributions.
comment: Built with the Johnson–Wehrly construction, it couples the speed and direction marginals through a circular dependence density; it is used to model the joint wind speed–direction regime for wind resource assessment.
distributionFormula: f(v,θ) = 2π g(ζ) f_V(v) f_Θ(θ), with ζ = 2π[F_V(v) − F_Θ(θ)]
distributionParameters: f_V, F_V: PDF and CDF of the inverse-Gaussian–lognormal wind-speed mixture ; f_Θ, F_Θ: PDF and CDF of the six-component von Mises direction mixture ; g(ζ): circular density of the linking variable ζ

modelName: angular-linear truncated-normal-Weibull distribution with 3 von Mises components
definition: An angular-linear joint distribution of wind speed and wind direction that uses a truncated-normal–Weibull mixture for wind speed and three-component von Mises mixtures for wind direction and the circular linking variable.
comment: It is built with the Johnson–Wehrly construction, linking the linear and circular marginals through a circular density of the difference of their cumulative distributions; it is used to model joint wind speed–direction behaviour for wind resource assessment.
distributionFormula: f(v,θ) = 2π g(ζ) f_V(v) f_Θ(θ), ζ = 2π[F_V(v) − F_Θ(θ)], with f_V a truncated-normal–Weibull mixture and f_Θ and g mixtures of three von Mises densities
distributionParameters: f_V: truncated-normal–Weibull wind-speed marginal ; f_Θ: von Mises mixture wind-direction marginal ; g: von Mises mixture density of the circular variable ζ ; F_V, F_Θ: marginal cumulative distribution functions

modelName: angular-linear truncated-normal-Weibull distribution with 6 von Mises components
definition: An angular-linear joint probability distribution of wind speed and wind direction whose linear marginal is a truncated-normal-Weibull mixture and whose circular marginal is a mixture of six von Mises distributions.
comment: It is built with the Johnson-Wehrly construction, linking the two marginals through a circular dependence density, and is used to model the joint occurrence of wind speed and direction for wind resource assessment.
distributionFormula: f(v,θ) = 2π g(ζ) f_V(v) f_Θ(θ), with ζ = 2π[F_V(v) − F_Θ(θ)] ; f_V(v) = ω/(I σ √(2π)) exp[−(v−μ)²/(2σ²)] + (1−ω)(k/c)(v/c)^(k−1) exp[−(v/c)^k] ; f_Θ(θ) = Σ_{j=1}^{6} w_j exp[κ_j cos(θ−μ_j)]/(2π I0(κ_j))
distributionParameters: f_V, F_V: pdf and cdf of the truncated-normal-Weibull wind-speed model ; ω: mixing weight ; μ, σ: truncated-normal mean and standard deviation ; I: normalising factor of the truncated normal ; k: Weibull shape parameter ; c: Weibull scale parameter ; f_Θ, F_Θ: pdf and cdf of the wind-direction von Mises mixture ; w_j: weights ; μ_j: mean directions ; κ_j: concentration parameters ; g(ζ): circular density linking speed and direction

definition: The anisotropic lognormal model is a bivariate joint distribution of wind speed and direction built from independent longitudinal and lateral wind-speed components each following a three-parameter lognormal law.
comment: Transforming the two component distributions to polar coordinates yields the joint density of wind speed and direction, used to describe directional wind regimes in wind-resource assessment.

definition: A hybrid model in which an artificial neural network is trained or calibrated using the simulated annealing metaheuristic.
comment: Simulated annealing explores the network weight or hyperparameter space with a decreasing temperature schedule to avoid local minima; it is used to improve neural-network prediction of renewable-energy variables such as solar radiation.

definition: A temperature-based empirical solar radiation model that extends the Hargreaves-Samani equation with an elevation correction factor.
comment: It estimates global solar radiation from the daily temperature range and extraterrestrial radiation, adjusting the Hargreaves coefficient for site altitude, and is used where only air temperature records are available.
empiricalModelParameters: Rs: global solar radiation ; kRs: empirical Hargreaves coefficient ; z: site elevation (m) ; Tmax: maximum air temperature ; Tmin: minimum air temperature ; Ra: extraterrestrial radiation
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Sites with temperature data only; accounts for elevation effects

definition: An annual Budyko water-balance model is a hydrological model that partitions long-term precipitation into evapotranspiration and runoff using a Budyko-type curve.
comment: Actual evapotranspiration is estimated from the aridity index (here with the Choudhury formulation), runoff is obtained as the residual assuming negligible storage change, and local discharge is routed through the river network; it is used to estimate river discharge for large-scale hydropower potential.

definition: A physical model that computes annual electricity generation from the technical power of a plant and its annual operating time.
comment: Annual energy is obtained as power multiplied by the number of operating hours in a year, here taken as 97% of the 8760 hours; it is used to estimate the energy yield of renewable plants.
physicalModelParameters: E: annual energy generation ; P_t: technical power ; 0.97: annual operating-time fraction ; 8760: hours per year
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: energy as the time integral of power

definition: An empirical calculation that estimates the annual energy production of a renewable-energy deployment scenario from pixel-level capacity factors, areas and array densities after losses.
comment: Capacity factors and suitable areas are aggregated over all candidate pixels and corrected for losses to give scenario-level energy yield; it is used in spatial renewable-energy potential assessments.
empiricalModelParameters: CF_p ; A_p ; η ; ρ_L

definition: Aquila-optimized support vector regression is a hybrid model in which the hyperparameters of a support vector regression are tuned by the Aquila Optimizer metaheuristic.
comment: The Aquila Optimizer, inspired by the hunting behaviour of eagles, searches penalty and kernel parameters that minimize SVR error; it is applied to forecasting renewable-energy variables.

definition: A hybrid model in which the hyperparameters of an XGBoost gradient-boosting regressor are tuned by the Aquila Optimizer metaheuristic.
comment: The Aquila Optimizer searches the XGBoost hyperparameter space to minimise prediction error; it is used to improve forecasts of renewable-energy variables such as solar radiation or power output.

definition: A physics-inspired population-based metaheuristic optimization algorithm modelled on Archimedes principle of buoyancy.
comment: Candidate solutions are treated as immersed objects with density, volume and acceleration that are updated through simulated collisions until equilibrium; it is used to tune model parameters or solve sizing and dispatch problems in renewable-energy systems.

definition: The area ratio method is an empirical regionalization technique that transfers streamflow from a gauged donor catchment to a hydrologically similar ungauged catchment by scaling with catchment area (and optionally rainfall).
comment: Flows at the donor gauge are multiplied by the ratio of drainage areas (and here mean rainfall) of the two catchments; it is used to estimate discharge at ungauged small-hydropower sites.
empiricalModelParameters: Q_u: streamflow at the ungauged site ; Q_g: streamflow at the gauged site ; A_u, A_g: drainage areas of ungauged and gauged catchments ; P_u, P_g: mean rainfall of ungauged and gauged catchments
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: hydrologically similar, nearby catchments of comparable size

definition: A machine learning model composed of layers of interconnected artificial neurons that map inputs to outputs through weighted sums and nonlinear activation functions.
comment: Weights are learned by backpropagation on training data; ANNs are used to predict and forecast solar radiation, wind speed and power output.

definition: A physics-based aero-hydro-servo-elastic simulation of wind-turbine power production using the ASHES software.
comment: It couples aerodynamic loads computed from the incoming wind with structural dynamics and turbine control to simulate power output; it is used to estimate turbine production from measured or modelled wind speeds.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: blade element momentum theory coupled with multibody structural dynamics

definition: An autoencoder-based regression model is a neural network that uses an encoder to learn a compact latent representation of the inputs and a regression layer to predict a continuous target.
comment: The encoder compresses high-dimensional or noisy inputs into informative features before regression, and is used to predict variables such as power output or resource potential.

definition: A linear stochastic time-series model that combines autoregressive and moving-average terms applied to a differenced series.
comment: Differencing removes non-stationarity and the remaining series is modelled as a linear function of its past values and past forecast errors; it is used to forecast solar irradiance, temperature, wind speed and energy production.
timeSeriesModelFormula: φ(B) (1 − B)^d X_t = c + θ(B) ε_t, with φ(B) = 1 − φ1 B − … − φp B^p and θ(B) = 1 + θ1 B + … + θq B^q
timeSeriesModelParameters: p: autoregressive order ; d: degree of differencing ; q: moving-average order ; φi: autoregressive coefficients ; θj: moving-average coefficients ; c: constant ; B: backshift operator ; ε_t: white-noise error

modelName: autoregressive integrated moving average - nonlinear regression hybrid model
definition: A hybrid forecasting model that combines an ARIMA model of cloud cover with nonlinear regressions of global horizontal irradiance.
comment: ARIMA predicts cloud-cover transients and irradiance is then obtained from regressions conditioned on solar zenith angle and cloud condition, for short-term solar irradiance forecasting.

modelName: autoregressive integrated moving average with exogenous variables
definition: ARIMAX is a time-series model that extends ARIMA with a linear term for exogenous explanatory variables.
comment: The differenced series is modelled as autoregressive and moving-average components plus a regression on external predictors; in renewable-energy studies it serves as a forecasting baseline, here with precipitation as exogenous input for streamflow or hydropower.
timeSeriesModelFormula: φ(B)(1 − B)^d y_t = β x_t + θ(B) ε_t
timeSeriesModelParameters: p: autoregressive order ; d: degree of differencing ; q: moving-average order ; φ(B): AR polynomial ; θ(B): MA polynomial ; β: coefficients of exogenous variables x_t ; ε_t: white-noise error ; B: backshift operator

modelName: autoregressive moving average and autoregressive integrated moving average multi-month model set
definition: A set of autoregressive moving average and autoregressive integrated moving average time-series models fitted to monthly mean daily global solar radiation.
comment: The models express radiation as a linear function of past values and past errors, with differencing for non-stationary series; they are used to predict monthly global solar radiation.
timeSeriesModelFormula: φ(B)(1 − B)^d X_t = c + θ(B) ε_t, with φ(B) = 1 − φ1 B − ... − φp B^p and θ(B) = 1 + θ1 B + ... + θq B^q
timeSeriesModelParameters: p: autoregressive order ; d: degree of differencing ; q: moving-average order ; φi: autoregressive coefficients ; θj: moving-average coefficients ; c: constant ; B: backshift operator ; ε_t: white-noise error

modelName: autoregressive moving average - artificial neural network hybrid model
definition: A hybrid forecasting model that combines a linear autoregressive moving average model with a nonlinear artificial neural network.
comment: The ARMA component captures linear autocorrelation while the neural network models the remaining nonlinear structure, often fitted on the ARMA residuals; it is used to forecast wind speed and solar radiation series.

modelName: autoregressive moving average - multilayer perceptron hybrid model
definition: The ARMA-MLP hybrid model is a forecasting model that combines an autoregressive moving-average model with a multilayer perceptron neural network.
comment: The ARMA component captures the linear structure of the stationary series while the MLP models nonlinear relations with exogenous inputs such as numerical weather predictions; it is used for solar and wind forecasting.

modelName: autoregressive moving average - nonlinear autoregressive neural network hybrid model
definition: A hybrid forecasting model that combines a linear autoregressive moving-average model with a nonlinear autoregressive neural network.
comment: The ARMA component captures the linear structure of the series and the NAR neural network models the nonlinear residual dynamics; it is used for short-term forecasting of solar or wind resource time series.

definition: A multilayer feedforward artificial neural network trained with the error back-propagation algorithm.
comment: Weights are adjusted by gradient descent on the output error propagated backward through the layers; it is widely used as a benchmark for predicting solar radiation, wind speed and power output.

definition: bagEarthGCV is a bagged ensemble of multivariate adaptive regression splines (MARS) whose pruning is selected by generalized cross-validation.
comment: Several MARS models are fitted on bootstrap resamples and their predictions are averaged to reduce variance; it is used for regression and forecasting of renewable-energy variables such as solar radiation.

definition: An ensemble regression model that averages the predictions of base regressors trained on bootstrap resamples of the training data.
comment: Bagging reduces variance by aggregating base learners such as support vector regression, neural networks and decision trees; it is applied to predicting renewable-energy variables.

definition: A neural network whose weights are treated as probability distributions and inferred with Bayesian methods.
comment: Bayesian inference regularises the network, quantifies predictive uncertainty and supports evidence-based architecture and input selection such as automatic relevance determination; it is used to predict solar radiation and other energy variables.

definition: A Bayesian-regularized neural network is a feedforward neural network whose weights are trained with Bayesian regularization that penalizes large weights to improve generalization.
comment: Training typically uses Levenberg-Marquardt optimization with a Bayesian-determined weight-decay term, reducing overfitting on small datasets; it is used for instance to estimate PV module temperature or power.

definition: A two-parameter continuous probability distribution defined on the interval [0, 1].
comment: Its two shape parameters allow flexible unimodal, U-shaped or skewed densities on a bounded interval; it is used for bounded variables such as the clearness index or normalized solar radiation.
distributionParameters: α: first shape parameter ; β: second shape parameter ; B(α, β): beta function

definition: A regression model for response variables bounded in the open interval (0,1) that assumes a beta-distributed response.
comment: The mean of the beta-distributed response is linked to predictors through a link function such as the logit and parameters are estimated by maximum likelihood; it is used for bounded quantities such as capacity factors.

definition: A bidirectional long short-term memory network is a recurrent neural network that combines two LSTM layers processing a sequence in forward and backward directions.
comment: Concatenating forward and backward hidden states lets the model use past and future context within an input window; it is used to forecast wind speed, solar irradiance and power output.

definition: A regression model that relates a binary outcome to explanatory variables through the logistic function of a linear predictor.
comment: Coefficients are estimated by maximum likelihood and interpreted as log-odds; it is used to analyse determinants of renewable-energy technology adoption.

definition: A two-parameter continuous probability distribution for positive, right-skewed data originally derived from fatigue-failure processes.
comment: Its shape and scale parameters are fitted to observed data by maximum likelihood or moments; it is used as a candidate law for wind-speed frequency distributions.
distributionParameters: a: shape parameter ; b: scale parameter

definition: Boosting ensemble regression is a machine learning ensemble that sequentially combines base regressors so that each new learner corrects the errors of the previous ones.
comment: Base learners such as support vector regressors, neural networks or decision trees are reweighted iteratively and aggregated into a stronger predictor of continuous renewable-energy variables.

definition: A wrapper feature-selection algorithm that uses random-forest importance scores compared against randomized shadow features to identify all relevant input variables.
comment: Each feature is compared with permuted shadow copies over repeated random-forest runs and retained only if significantly more important; it is used as a preprocessing step to select predictors for solar-radiation models such as SVR.

definition: A non-seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average model identified, estimated and checked following the Box-Jenkins methodology.
comment: The series is differenced to stationarity and modelled with autoregressive and moving-average terms selected through identification, estimation and diagnostic checking; it is used to forecast meteorological variables, solar radiation and PV module temperature.
timeSeriesModelFormula: φ(B)(1 − B)^d y_t = c + θ(B) ε_t, with φ(B) = 1 − φ_1B − … − φ_pB^p and θ(B) = 1 + θ_1B + … + θ_qB^q
timeSeriesModelParameters: p: autoregressive order ; d: degree of differencing ; q: moving-average order ; φ_i: autoregressive coefficients ; θ_j: moving-average coefficients ; c: constant ; ε_t: white-noise error ; B: backshift operator

definition: The Bristow–Campbell model is an empirical temperature-based model that estimates daily global solar radiation from the daily air-temperature range.
comment: Atmospheric transmittance is expressed as an exponential function of the diurnal temperature range; it is used to estimate solar radiation where sunshine or radiation measurements are lacking.
empiricalModelParameters: H: daily global solar radiation ; H0: daily extraterrestrial radiation ; ΔT: daily air-temperature range ; a, b, c: empirical coefficients
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: daily time scale; coefficients calibrated locally

definition: A physical model that simulates the power output of the BTPS6500 wind turbine as a piecewise function of hub-height wind speed.
comment: Power is zero below the cut-in and above the cut-off speed, rises between cut-in and rated speed and is constant at rated power up to cut-off, with Weibull parameters extrapolated from 10 m to hub height; it is used to estimate turbine energy yield at a site.
physicalModelParameters: v_c: cut-in wind speed ; v_r: rated wind speed ; v_f: cut-off wind speed ; P_r: rated power ; k: Weibull shape parameter ; c: Weibull scale parameter
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: conversion of wind kinetic energy flux described by the turbine power curve

definition: A three-parameter continuous probability distribution for positive data, also known as the Burr type XII or Singh-Maddala distribution.
comment: Its two shape parameters and one scale parameter give flexible tails, and it is fitted to wind-speed frequency data as an alternative to the Weibull law.
distributionParameters: a: shape parameter ; b: scale parameter ; k: shape parameter

definition: The Burr-GEV mixture distribution is a two-component finite mixture probability distribution that combines a three-parameter Burr distribution and a generalized extreme value distribution.
comment: The weighted sum of the two components captures bimodal or heavy-tailed wind-speed regimes better than single distributions; parameters are usually estimated by maximum likelihood or metaheuristics.
distributionParameters: ω: mixing weight ; α: Burr first shape parameter ; k: Burr second shape parameter ; β: Burr scale parameter ; μ: GEV location parameter ; σ: GEV scale parameter ; ξ: GEV shape parameter

modelName: CALORIUS 37 wind-turbine power and energy calculation
definition: A study-specific wind-turbine power and energy calculation for the CALORIUS 37 turbine that combines wind-power relations, air-density correction, height extrapolation and the turbine power curve.
comment: Wind speed is extrapolated to hub height, corrected for local air density and converted to power through the CALORIUS 37 power curve and turbine efficiency; it is used to estimate average power and annual energy production at a site.
physicalModelParameters: \bar{P}: average turbine power; P(v_i): CALORIUS 37 power-curve value at wind speed v_i; H(v_i): wind-speed frequency/probability; v_d: cut-in speed; v_a: cut-out speed; E_w: annual energy; N: number of hours
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: CALORIUS 37 manufacturer power curve is combined with the wind-speed frequency distribution to estimate average power, then annual energy is N times average power.

modelName: Cameroon quadratic diffuse solar radiation model
definition: A location-specific empirical model that relates the diffuse fraction of solar radiation to the clearness index through a quadratic polynomial calibrated for Cameroon.
comment: Regression coefficients fitted on local measurements give the diffuse-to-global radiation ratio from the clearness index, allowing diffuse radiation to be estimated from global radiation at Cameroonian sites.
empiricalModelFormula: Hd/H = a + b Kt + c Kt²
empiricalModelParameters: Hd: diffuse solar radiation ; H: global solar radiation ; Kt: clearness index ; a, b, c: site-specific regression coefficients
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Calibrated for Cameroonian sites

definition: The Capderou method is a semi-empirical clear-sky model that estimates global, direct and diffuse solar irradiance on horizontal and inclined surfaces from atmospheric turbidity.
comment: It computes beam and diffuse components using a Linke-type turbidity factor derived from site and seasonal parameters; it is used for solar-resource estimation and collector design, notably in North African and Sahelian studies.

definition: A gradient boosting model on oblivious decision trees that natively handles categorical features with ordered target statistics.
comment: CatBoost builds trees sequentially to correct previous errors while reducing prediction shift; it is used to predict solar radiation components such as diffuse radiation.

definition: A mathematical technique that derives the probability distribution of a transformed random variable from the distribution of the original variable.
comment: It uses the inverse transformation and its Jacobian to obtain the new density, for example to derive wind power density distributions from wind-speed distributions; it is a method rather than a model.

definition: Chaos Game Optimization is a population-based metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by chaos theory and the chaos game for constructing fractals.
comment: Candidate solutions are moved toward seeds defined by the best solution and group means following fractal self-similarity rules; it is used to tune models and estimate parameters such as PV cell or distribution parameters.

definition: A decision-tree learning algorithm that recursively partitions the predictor space with binary splits to produce classification or regression trees.
comment: Splits are chosen to minimise impurity or squared error and leaves hold constant predictions; in renewable-energy studies it is used as a benchmark for forecasting solar radiation and power output.

definition: A Kyoto Protocol flexibility mechanism that issues certified emission reductions to emission-reduction projects in non-Annex I countries.
comment: It allows projects such as renewable-energy plants in developing countries to earn tradable carbon credits if their emission reductions are additional; it is a policy instrument rather than a model.

definition: A clearness-index power exergy model is an empirical power-law correlation that estimates the exergy-efficiency factor of solar radiation from the clearness index.
comment: The exergy factor of global solar radiation is regressed on the clearness index with a power-function form; it is used in solar-exergy studies to estimate exergy content where detailed spectral data are unavailable.
empiricalModelParameters: \eta_{go}: global solar-radiation exergy-efficiency factor; k_t: clearness index

definition: A Box–Jenkins transfer-function time-series model that uses cloud cover as an exogenous input series.
comment: The output series is modelled as a rational lag function of the input plus an ARMA noise term; it is used to forecast solar radiation at high temporal resolution.
timeSeriesModelParameters: Y_t: output series ; X_t: exogenous input (cloud cover) ; ω(B): numerator lag polynomial ; δ(B): denominator lag polynomial ; b: input delay ; θ(B), φ(B): noise moving-average and autoregressive polynomials ; B: backshift operator ; ε_t: white noise

definition: A hybrid model in which multivariate adaptive regression splines are optimised by the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy.
comment: The evolution strategy tunes the MARS configuration or inputs to improve accuracy; it is used to predict renewable-energy variables such as solar radiation.

definition: CMA-ES-XGB is a hybrid model in which the hyperparameters of an extreme gradient boosting model are tuned by the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy.
comment: CMA-ES adapts a multivariate normal search distribution to find XGBoost settings that minimize validation error; it is used for predicting renewable-energy variables such as solar radiation or wind power.

definition: An empirical model that estimates hourly global solar irradiation from daily totals as a function of hour angle and sunset hour angle.
comment: It gives the ratio of hourly to daily global irradiation through a cosine-type function of solar time whose coefficients depend on the sunset hour angle and hence on the day of year; it is used to disaggregate daily solar radiation into hourly values.
empiricalModelFormula: r_t = (π/24) (a + b cos ω) (cos ω − cos ωs) / (sin ωs − (π ωs/180) cos ωs), with a = 0.409 + 0.5016 sin(ωs − 60°) and b = 0.6609 − 0.4767 sin(ωs − 60°)
empiricalModelParameters: r_t: ratio of hourly to daily global irradiation ; ω: hour angle at the midpoint of the hour (degrees) ; ωs: sunset hour angle (degrees) ; a, b: coefficients depending on ωs
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Clear to moderately cloudy conditions; requires daily global irradiation totals

definition: A coupled global climate model developed by NCAR that couples atmosphere, ocean, land and sea-ice components.
comment: CCSM4 simulates the global climate system and contributed projections to CMIP5; its outputs are used to assess future changes in wind, solar and hydrological resources.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Coupled climate-system model used for climate projections.

definition: The Community Earth System Model is a fully coupled global Earth-system model simulating atmosphere, ocean, land, sea ice and biogeochemistry.
comment: Developed by NCAR, its CESM2 version contributes to CMIP6; its projections are used to assess climate-change impacts on wind, solar and hydropower resources.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Coupled Earth-system model used for climate projections.

modelName: complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise
definition: A signal decomposition method that splits a non-stationary series into intrinsic mode functions by adding adaptive white noise to repeated empirical mode decompositions.
comment: CEEMDAN is a preprocessing step that reduces mode mixing before each component is forecast separately; it is used in hybrid solar and wind forecasting pipelines.

definition: A data-assimilation scheme for hydrodynamic river models that uses proportional-integral-derivative controllers to correct simulated water levels toward observations.
comment: The difference between observed and simulated water levels is converted by PID controllers into correction discharges added as fictive lateral inflows; it improves river flow and water-level forecasts relevant to hydropower operation.
physicalModelParameters: Q_corr: corrective flow; e(t): observed-minus-simulated water-level error; K_p: proportional gain; K_i: integral gain; K_d: derivative gain

definition: A convolutional long short-term memory network is a recurrent neural network in which the input-to-state and state-to-state transitions of the LSTM cell are convolution operations.
comment: ConvLSTM captures spatial and temporal dependencies jointly and is used for spatiotemporal forecasting of variables such as solar irradiance, wind speed or power.

definition: A deep neural network that uses convolutional layers with shared learnable filters to extract local features from grid-structured or sequential data.
comment: Stacked convolution and pooling layers learn hierarchical patterns that feed dense output layers; it is used to predict solar radiation, wind speed and power from meteorological time series or satellite images.

modelName: convolutional neural network - dual-stage stacked regression - support vector machine hybrid model
definition: A hybrid stacked-ensemble model combining a convolutional neural network, dual-stage stacked regression and a support vector machine meta-learner.
comment: CNN-derived features and base regressors feed a two-stage stacking scheme whose level-1 learner is an SVM tuned with HyperOpt, for renewable-energy prediction tasks such as solar radiation forecasting.

modelName: convolutional neural network - Gaussian process regression hybrid model
definition: A CNN–GPR hybrid model is a combined model in which features extracted by a convolutional neural network are used as inputs to Gaussian process regression.
comment: The CNN learns spatial or temporal features and the GPR provides nonlinear probabilistic predictions with uncertainty estimates; it is used for forecasting solar radiation or renewable power.

modelName: convolutional neural network - multilayer perceptron - Gaussian process regression hybrid model
definition: A hybrid model that chains a convolutional neural network, a multilayer perceptron and Gaussian process regression.
comment: The CNN extracts features, the MLP learns nonlinear structure and the GPR produces predictions with uncertainty intervals; it is used for probabilistic prediction of renewable-energy variables.

modelName: convolutional neural network - multilayer perceptron hybrid model
definition: A hybrid deep-learning model in which convolutional layers extract features that are passed to a multilayer perceptron for prediction.
comment: The convolutional part learns local patterns in the inputs and the perceptron maps them to the target; it is used to forecast solar radiation, wind speed or power output.

modelName: Coordinated Regional Climate Downscaling Experiment Africa 15-regional climate model ensemble
definition: The CORDEX-Africa 15-RCM ensemble is a multi-model ensemble of fifteen regional climate model simulations over Africa produced within the Coordinated Regional Climate Downscaling Experiment.
comment: Regional models dynamically downscale global climate models under emission scenarios such as RCP4.5 and RCP8.5, and the ensemble provides projections of precipitation and temperature used to assess climate impacts on hydropower and other renewables.

definition: A European Copernicus service that provides atmospheric-composition analyses, forecasts and reanalyses, including satellite-based solar-radiation estimates.
comment: It combines numerical atmospheric modelling with satellite observations through data assimilation to produce aerosol, ozone and surface solar irradiance products; it is used as a reference or predictor dataset in solar resource assessment.

definition: A genetic programming approach for symbolic regression whose input selection is supported by coplot multivariate analysis.
comment: Genetic programming evolves explicit mathematical expressions relating inputs to the target, with coplot used to visualize and select relevant variables; it is used to estimate solar radiation from meteorological data.

definition: CRO–ELM is a hybrid model in which the Coral Reefs Optimization metaheuristic evolves the weights or structure of an Extreme Learning Machine.
comment: The bio-inspired optimizer searches the ELM input weights to improve the network accuracy; it is used for daily global solar radiation prediction.

definition: A hybrid model that fuses a support vector machine estimating global solar radiation with a second support vector machine estimating its error through a weighted sum.
comment: The error-estimating SVM corrects the primary estimate to improve accuracy; it is used to estimate global solar radiation.

definition: A derivative-free evolutionary optimisation algorithm that samples candidate solutions from a multivariate normal distribution whose covariance matrix is adapted during the search.
comment: It updates the mean, step size and covariance of the sampling distribution from the best candidates; it is used to tune parameters of predictive and energy-system models.

definition: A cubic polynomial turbine power curve is an empirical model that represents wind turbine power output as a third-degree polynomial of wind speed fitted to manufacturer power-curve data.
comment: The coefficients are obtained by least-squares fitting to the turbine performance curve and the model is used to estimate turbine output and energy yield from wind-speed data.
empiricalModelParameters: P: turbine power output ; v: wind speed ; a0, a1, a2, a3: fitted polynomial coefficients
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Valid between cut-in and rated wind speeds of the fitted turbine

definition: A polynomial regression model in which the response is expressed as a third-degree polynomial of the predictor.
comment: Coefficients of the linear, quadratic and cubic terms are estimated by least squares; it is used to fit seasonal or nonlinear relationships between solar radiation and meteorological variables.

definition: A piecewise cubic polynomial interpolation of manufacturer wind-turbine power-curve data.
comment: Cubic polynomials with continuous first and second derivatives are fitted between successive power-curve points to estimate turbine power output at any wind speed, used in wind energy yield assessment.
empiricalModelFormula: P(v) = a_i + b_i (v − v_i) + c_i (v − v_i)² + d_i (v − v_i)³ for v_i ≤ v ≤ v_(i+1)
empiricalModelParameters: P: turbine power output ; v: wind speed ; v_i: tabulated power-curve wind speeds ; a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i: spline coefficients of interval i
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Within the range of manufacturer power-curve data, between cut-in and cut-out wind speeds

definition: Cubist is a rule-based regression model tree that fits multivariate linear models at the terminal rules of a decision tree.
comment: It derives rules from a pruned model tree, smooths predictions across levels and can be combined in committees with instance-based corrections; it is used to predict solar radiation and other renewable-energy variables.

modelName: Cuckoo Search–Optimally Pruned Extreme Learning Machine
definition: A hybrid model in which the Cuckoo Search metaheuristic optimises an optimally pruned extreme learning machine.
comment: It is applied with direct and direct-recursive multi-step strategies to forecast renewable-energy time series such as solar radiation.

definition: An empirical rainfall-runoff method of the US Natural Resources Conservation Service that estimates direct runoff from rainfall and a curve number characterising soil and land cover.
comment: The curve number determines the potential maximum retention, from which runoff depth and peak discharge are computed; it is used in hydrological assessments of catchments for small hydropower and water resources.
empiricalModelFormula: Q = (P − Ia)² / (P − Ia + S) for P > Ia, else Q = 0 ; Ia = 0.2 S ; S = 25400/CN − 254
empiricalModelParameters: Q: direct runoff depth (mm) ; P: rainfall depth (mm) ; Ia: initial abstraction (mm) ; S: potential maximum retention (mm) ; CN: curve number
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Event-based runoff estimation in small to medium ungauged catchments; CN from soil group, land use and antecedent moisture

definition: The Dagum-GEV mixture distribution is a two-component finite mixture probability distribution that combines a three-parameter Dagum distribution and a generalized extreme value distribution.
comment: The weighted combination models multimodal and heavy-tailed wind-speed distributions; its parameters are typically estimated by maximum likelihood and compared with single and other mixture laws.
distributionParameters: ω: mixing weight ; a: Dagum first shape parameter ; k: Dagum second shape parameter ; b: Dagum scale parameter ; μ: GEV location parameter ; σ: GEV scale parameter ; ξ: GEV shape parameter

definition: A two-component heterogeneous mixture distribution composed of a Dagum and a Weibull probability density.
comment: A weight parameter combines the two component densities so that the mixture can capture bimodal or heavy-tailed wind-speed regimes; it is used to fit wind-speed frequency distributions and estimate wind power density.
distributionParameters: w: mixing weight ; a: Dagum shape parameter ; p: Dagum second shape parameter ; b: Dagum scale parameter ; k: Weibull shape parameter ; c: Weibull scale parameter

definition: A non-parametric linear-programming method that measures the relative efficiency of decision-making units with multiple inputs and outputs.
comment: Each unit is compared to an efficient frontier built from observed units by solving a linear program (e.g. the output-oriented BCC model under variable returns to scale); it is used to evaluate the efficiency or environmental impact of renewable-energy projects.

definition: A decision tree is a supervised machine-learning model that recursively partitions the input space into regions by threshold rules and assigns a prediction to each leaf.
comment: Splits are chosen to minimize impurity or variance, giving interpretable rules; it is used to estimate solar radiation, wind power and other renewable-energy quantities.

definition: A machine learning model based on neural networks with multiple hidden layers that learn hierarchical representations of the data.
comment: Deep networks are trained by backpropagation on large datasets; they are used to estimate and forecast solar radiation and wind quantities.

definition: A feedforward artificial neural network with several hidden layers.
comment: Stacked densely connected layers, possibly with dropout, learn nonlinear mappings from inputs to targets; it is used to predict solar radiation, wind speed and renewable power output.

definition: The delta change method is an empirical climate-downscaling technique that perturbs observed climate series with the change signal simulated by a climate model between a reference and a future period.
comment: Multiplicative factors for precipitation and additive shifts for temperature derived from regional climate models are applied to observations, and the perturbed series drive hydrological models to assess future discharge and hydropower potential.
empiricalModelFormula: P_fut = P_obs × (P_RCM,fut / P_RCM,ref) ; T_fut = T_obs + (T_RCM,fut − T_RCM,ref)
empiricalModelParameters: P_obs, T_obs: observed precipitation and temperature ; P_RCM,ref, T_RCM,ref: climate-model values in the reference period ; P_RCM,fut, T_RCM,fut: climate-model values in the future period
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Assumes the climate-model bias is constant between reference and future periods and that the temporal variability pattern of observations is preserved

definition: A geospatial assessment procedure that derives potential gross hydraulic head from a digital elevation model and stream network and checks it against Google Earth and handheld GPS elevations.
comment: Elevation drops along stream reaches are extracted from the DEM and compared with Google Earth and GPS measurements; it is used to identify and validate candidate small-hydropower sites.

modelName: deployment-responsive feed-in tariff with breathing cap
definition: A technology-specific feed-in tariff policy design whose tariff degression adjusts automatically to deployment relative to planned capacity.
comment: Tariffs decrease on a schedule and are corrected up or down when installations exceed or fall short of a deployment corridor, a policy instrument for controlling renewable-energy support costs rather than a model.

definition: A doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) is a variable-speed wound-rotor induction machine whose rotor is connected to the grid through back-to-back power converters.
comment: The rotor- and grid-side converters control slip power, allowing variable-speed operation and reactive-power control; it is widely used as the generator technology of modern wind turbines.

definition: A non-parametric kernel density estimator obtained as the solution of a diffusion partial differential equation on a finite domain.
comment: The heat-equation formulation provides automatic bandwidth selection and boundary correction and is computed efficiently with the discrete cosine transform; it is used to model wind-speed distributions.
distributionFormula: f̂(x;t) solves ∂f̂/∂t = ½ ∂²f̂/∂x² on a bounded domain with Neumann boundary conditions and initial condition f̂(x;0) = (1/n) Σ δ(x − x_i)
distributionParameters: t: diffusion time (squared bandwidth) ; x_i: sample observations ; n: sample size

definition: A one-dimensional hydrodynamic model that solves the diffusive-wave simplification of the Saint-Venant equations for open-channel flow.
comment: It neglects convective acceleration and uses a staggered numerical scheme to compute water levels and discharges along channels; it is used for river flow simulation and forecasting.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: One-dimensional Saint-Venant continuity and momentum equations solved with a diffusion-wave simplification; convective acceleration is neglected.

definition: The Duffie and Beckman model is an empirical expression that estimates extraterrestrial solar irradiance on a plane normal to the beam as a function of the day of the year.
comment: It corrects the solar constant for the eccentricity of the Earth orbit and is used as the basis for computing extraterrestrial radiation in solar-resource estimation.
empiricalModelParameters: G_on: extraterrestrial irradiance on a plane normal to the beam ; G_sc: solar constant ; n: day of the year

definition: A European community Earth-system model that couples atmosphere, ocean, sea-ice and land-surface components for global climate simulation.
comment: It is built around the ECMWF IFS atmosphere and NEMO ocean models and contributes to CMIP5 and CMIP6 projections; its outputs are used to assess future changes in wind, solar and hydropower resources.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Earth-system/climate model used to provide climate projections.

definition: A reservoir-computing recurrent neural network with a fixed sparse random recurrent reservoir in which only the output weights are trained.
comment: Inputs drive the high-dimensional reservoir dynamics and a linear readout is fitted, usually by ridge regression, giving fast training; it is used for wind speed, wind power and solar irradiance time-series forecasting.

definition: Eclat is an unsupervised association-rule mining algorithm that finds frequent itemsets using a vertical transaction-identifier representation and set intersections.
comment: Frequent itemsets are found depth-first by intersecting transaction lists, from which association rules are derived; here it identifies relations between solar radiation and meteorological variables.

definition: A penalised linear regression model that combines L1 (lasso) and L2 (ridge) penalties on the coefficients.
comment: The mixed penalty performs variable selection while handling correlated predictors; it is used to predict renewable-energy quantities such as solar radiation.

definition: A wind-speed probability distribution derived from uncorrelated zero-mean Gaussian wind components with different variances.
comment: It describes the magnitude of a bivariate Gaussian vector with unequal component variances (Hoyt form) and generalises the Rayleigh law; it is used to model wind-speed frequencies.
distributionParameters: σu²: variance of the u wind component ; σv²: variance of the v wind component ; I0: modified Bessel function of the first kind of order zero

definition: ENLIL is a three-dimensional time-dependent magnetohydrodynamic model of the heliosphere that simulates solar-wind flow and coronal mass ejection propagation.
comment: Driven by coronal boundary conditions, it solves the ideal MHD equations from about 0.1 AU outward and is used operationally to forecast solar-wind conditions near Earth.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Three-dimensional heliospheric magnetohydrodynamic solar-wind model driven by coronal boundary conditions.

definition: A sequential Monte Carlo data-assimilation method that approximates the Kalman filter by representing the state error covariance with an ensemble of model realizations.
comment: Each ensemble member is propagated by the model and updated with observations using a covariance estimated from the ensemble; it is used to update hydrological states and parameters or improve forecasts of renewable-energy variables.

definition: A two-parameter continuous probability distribution of the sum of k independent exponential variables, equal to a gamma distribution with integer shape.
comment: Its probability density is defined by an integer shape and a rate parameter; it is among the candidate distributions fitted to wind speed frequency data.
distributionParameters: k: shape parameter (positive integer) ; λ: rate parameter

modelName: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Interim reanalysis
definition: ERA-Interim is a global atmospheric reanalysis produced by ECMWF that combines a numerical weather prediction model with data assimilation of observations (1979–2019).
comment: It provides gridded, consistent estimates of wind, radiation, temperature and precipitation; renewable-energy studies use it as a substitute or complement for station measurements.

modelName: European Hydrological Predictions for the Environment model
definition: A pan-European configuration of the semi-distributed HYPE hydrological model that simulates water flows across European catchments.
comment: It simulates discharge, snow, soil water and reservoir inflow at sub-basin scale; sub-models are used to provide inflow series for hydropower studies.

modelName: evolutionary particle filter - Markov-chain Monte Carlo hybrid data-assimilation model
definition: A hybrid data-assimilation approach combining an evolutionary particle filter with Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling for joint state and parameter estimation.
comment: Evolutionary operators maintain particle diversity while MCMC moves refine the posterior in high-dimensional problems; it is used to estimate states and parameters of hydrological models.

definition: The exponential distribution is a one-parameter continuous probability distribution with a monotonically decreasing density on the non-negative real line.
comment: It describes the frequency of variables such as wind speed or waiting times and serves as a simple benchmark against Weibull and other laws in wind-speed distribution fitting.
distributionParameters: λ: rate parameter (inverse of the mean)

definition: A Gaussian process regression model that uses an exponential covariance kernel.
comment: Predictions are obtained as the posterior mean of a Gaussian process whose covariance decays exponentially with input distance, providing uncertainty estimates; it is used to predict solar radiation and other renewable-energy variables.

definition: A continuous probability distribution obtained by exponentiating the cumulative distribution function of the epsilon distribution.
comment: It was introduced as a new flexible distribution and fitted to wind speed data as an alternative to the Weibull distribution.

definition: The exponentiated Weibull distribution is a three-parameter continuous distribution obtained by raising the two-parameter Weibull CDF to a positive power.
comment: The additional shape parameter allows monotone, bathtub and unimodal hazard shapes; it is used to fit wind-speed distributions more flexibly than the standard Weibull.
distributionParameters: a: shape parameter ; b: scale parameter ; γ: exponentiation shape parameter

definition: A three-parameter continuous distribution that extends the generalized Lindley distribution with two shape parameters and one scale parameter.
comment: It has an explicit cumulative distribution function and flexible hazard shapes; it is fitted to wind-speed data for wind resource assessment.
distributionFormula: f(x; α, θ, λ) = αθ²λ(1 + λx)^(2α − 1)·exp(θ − θ(1 + λx)^α) / (1 + θ), x > 0
distributionParameters: α: shape (α > 0) ; θ: shape/Lindley parameter (θ > 0) ; λ: scale-type parameter (λ > 0)

definition: A recursive state estimator for nonlinear dynamic systems that linearises the system and observation models around the current estimate.
comment: It alternates prediction and update steps using Jacobians to propagate means and covariances; it is used to estimate quantities such as PV module temperature and effective irradiance.

definition: Extreme gradient boosting is a gradient-boosted decision-tree ensemble algorithm with regularized objective and efficient parallel tree construction.
comment: Trees are added sequentially to fit the gradient of the loss with shrinkage and L1/L2 regularization; it is widely used to predict solar radiation, wind speed and renewable power output.

definition: A single-hidden-layer feedforward neural network whose input weights are randomly assigned and whose output weights are computed analytically by least squares.
comment: Avoiding iterative backpropagation makes training very fast; it is used to estimate daily global and diffuse solar radiation and to forecast wind speed.

definition: A bivariate distribution built with the Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern copula, joining two marginal distributions through a single association parameter.
comment: The joint density is the product of the marginals multiplied by a correction term weighted by the association parameter, allowing weak dependence; it is used to model the joint distribution of wind speed and wind direction.
distributionParameters: α: association parameter (−1 ≤ α ≤ 1) ; f_V, F_V: marginal pdf and cdf of wind speed ; f_Θ, F_Θ: marginal pdf and cdf of wind direction

definition: A Farlie–Gumbel–Morgenstern copula model for the joint distribution of wind speed and direction with an inverse-Gaussian–lognormal mixture speed marginal and a von Mises mixture direction marginal.
comment: The FGM copula links the two marginals through a single dependence parameter allowing weak positive or negative dependence; it is used to model the joint wind speed–direction regime.
distributionParameters: λ: FGM dependence parameter (−1 ≤ λ ≤ 1) ; f_V, F_V: PDF and CDF of the inverse-Gaussian–lognormal wind-speed mixture ; f_Θ, F_Θ: PDF and CDF of the von Mises mixture wind-direction model

definition: A Farlie–Gumbel–Morgenstern joint distribution of wind speed and wind direction with a truncated-normal–Weibull wind-speed marginal and a von Mises mixture wind-direction marginal.
comment: The FGM copula couples the marginals through a single dependence parameter allowing weak dependence; it is used to model joint wind speed–direction distributions.
distributionParameters: γ: dependence parameter in [−1, 1] ; f_V, F_V: truncated-normal–Weibull wind-speed density and distribution function ; f_Θ, F_Θ: von Mises mixture wind-direction density and distribution function

definition: An artificial neural network in which information flows in one direction from the input layer through hidden layers to the output layer.
comment: Weights are trained by backpropagation to map inputs to outputs; it is widely used as a benchmark to predict solar radiation, wind speed and power output.

definition: A fine Gaussian support vector machine is a support vector machine with a Gaussian radial basis function kernel using a small kernel scale, giving highly flexible decision boundaries.
comment: The small kernel scale allows fine detail to be captured at the risk of overfitting; it is used as one of several preset SVM learners compared for predicting renewable-energy variables.

definition: A two-parameter probability distribution whose cumulative distribution and density functions are derived using Finsler geometry.
comment: Its two parameters are fitted to observed data like other parametric laws; it was proposed as an alternative to classical distributions for modelling wind-speed frequency.
distributionParameters: C1 ; C2

definition: A hybrid model in which the weights or hyperparameters of an artificial neural network are optimized by the Firefly metaheuristic algorithm.
comment: The Firefly algorithm searches the network parameter space using attractiveness based on brightness, improving on gradient training; it is used as a benchmark for solar and wind prediction.

definition: A firefly-optimized random forest is a hybrid model in which the Firefly Algorithm tunes the hyperparameters of a random forest.
comment: The metaheuristic searches values such as the number of trees and leaf size to minimize prediction error; it is used for renewable-energy prediction such as solar radiation.

definition: A single-diode equivalent-circuit model of a photovoltaic cell defined by five parameters including series and shunt resistances.
comment: The current–voltage characteristic is computed from the photocurrent, diode saturation current, ideality factor, series and shunt resistance; it is used to predict PV cell and module power.
physicalModelFormula: I = I_ph − I_0 [exp((V + I R_s)/(n V_t)) − 1] − (V + I R_s)/R_sh
physicalModelParameters: I_ph: photocurrent ; I_0: diode saturation current ; n: diode ideality factor ; R_s: series resistance ; R_sh: shunt resistance ; V_t: thermal voltage kT/q
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: photovoltaic effect and Kirchhoff current law applied to the Shockley diode equation

definition: An empirical velocity-area method that estimates river discharge from the travel time of a floating object over a known distance.
comment: The surface velocity measured with the float is reduced by a correction coefficient to mean velocity and multiplied by the cross-sectional area; it is used for quick flow assessment at small hydropower sites.
empiricalModelParameters: Q: discharge ; k: surface-to-mean velocity correction coefficient ; L: travel distance ; t: travel time ; A: cross-sectional area
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Straight, uniform reach with steady flow and low wind

definition: A flow-duration curve is an empirical cumulative frequency curve that relates river discharge magnitude to the percentage of time that discharge is equalled or exceeded.
comment: Discharges are ranked in descending order and assigned exceedance probabilities; the curve is used to determine design flows and firm and average energy potential of hydropower sites.
empiricalModelParameters: P: exceedance probability (percent of time) ; m: rank of the discharge in descending order ; n: number of discharge observations
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Requires a sufficiently long discharge record representative of the flow regime

definition: A forward-backward greedy algorithm for learning sparse linear models by adaptively adding and removing features.
comment: Forward steps add the feature that most reduces the loss and backward steps remove features whose contribution has become small; it is used as a forecasting model for solar radiation in comparative machine-learning studies.

definition: A regression model that predicts the uncertainty of satellite-based solar forecasts from irradiance, cloud and weather-regime variables.
comment: It relates explanatory meteorological variables to the expected forecast error so that the reliability of each solar forecast can be anticipated.

definition: The gamma-Kumaraswamy distribution is a four-parameter continuous distribution generated by applying the gamma-generated family to the Kumaraswamy baseline distribution.
comment: Its additional shape parameters produce a wide variety of density shapes suitable for heterogeneous data; it is used to fit wind-speed distributions.
distributionParameters: x: normalized wind-speed variable in (0,1); a,b: Kumaraswamy parameters; \alpha,\beta: gamma parameters; \Gamma: gamma function

definition: A single-diode equivalent-circuit model of a photovoltaic cell defined by four parameters including a series resistance but no shunt resistance.
comment: The current–voltage characteristic is computed from the photocurrent, diode saturation current, ideality factor and series resistance; it is used to predict PV cell and module power.
physicalModelFormula: I = I_ph − I_0 [exp((V + I R_s)/(n V_t)) − 1]
physicalModelParameters: I_ph: photocurrent ; I_0: diode saturation current ; n: diode ideality factor ; R_s: series resistance ; V_t: thermal voltage kT/q
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: photovoltaic effect and Kirchhoff current law applied to the Shockley diode equation

definition: A study-specific empirical polynomial of fourth order that relates average wind speed to wind-turbine capacity factor.
comment: It is fitted to the relationship between site mean wind speed and capacity factor and then used to estimate capacity factors from wind speed.
empiricalModelParameters: u: average wind speed

definition: Fractional-area maximum power point tracking is an MPPT algorithm that uses fractional areas of the PV characteristic to drive a PV module to its maximum power point.
comment: It locates and stabilizes the operating point near maximum power by exploiting area relations of the current-voltage or power-voltage curve, as an alternative to perturb-and-observe methods.

definition: A two-parameter continuous probability distribution corresponding to the type II extreme value (inverse Weibull) distribution.
comment: Its heavy right tail makes it suitable for maxima and skewed positive data; it is fitted to wind-speed data to model the wind regime and estimate wind power density.
distributionParameters: k: shape parameter ; c: scale parameter

definition: An association-rule mining algorithm that discovers frequent itemsets using a compressed frequent-pattern tree without candidate generation.
comment: It builds an FP-tree and mines it recursively to find frequently co-occurring items; in renewable-energy forecasting it is used to select relevant input variables.

definition: Fuzzy ARAS is a multi-criteria decision-making method that extends the Additive Ratio Assessment with fuzzy numbers.
comment: Alternatives are ranked by the ratio of their aggregated fuzzy weighted performance to that of an ideal alternative; it is used to compare renewable-energy options or sites under uncertainty.

definition: A fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making method that combines the additive ratio assessment (ARAS) method with the utility and regret measures of VIKOR.
comment: Alternatives are scored with fuzzy linguistic ratings and ranked by combined ARAS and VIKOR measures; it is used to rank renewable-energy alternatives or sites.

definition: A soft clustering algorithm that assigns each data point a degree of membership to every cluster.
comment: It iteratively updates cluster centres and fuzzy memberships to minimise a weighted within-cluster distance; it is used to classify satellite-image pixels or group meteorological patterns in renewable-energy studies.

definition: A fuzzy inference system is a rule-based model that maps inputs to outputs through fuzzy membership functions, if-then rules and defuzzification.
comment: Inputs are fuzzified, combined through a rule base (e.g. Mamdani or Sugeno) and defuzzified to a crisp output; it is used as a benchmark for predicting solar radiation, wind power and other renewable-energy variables.

definition: A fuzzy extension of the PROMETHEE outranking multi-criteria decision method that handles imprecise criteria evaluations with fuzzy numbers.
comment: Alternatives are compared pairwise through fuzzy preference functions to compute positive, negative and net outranking flows; it is used to rank renewable-energy technologies, sites or policies.

definition: A fuzzy hybrid multi-criteria decision-making method combining PROMETHEE outranking and TOPSIS.
comment: It ranks alternatives under uncertain fuzzy judgements by integrating preference functions and distance to ideal solutions; it is used for renewable-energy technology or site selection.

definition: Fuzzy revised VIKOR is a fuzzy multi-criteria compromise-ranking method that modifies the VIKOR procedure for fuzzy evaluations.
comment: Alternatives are ranked by group utility and individual regret measures computed from fuzzy distances to ideal solutions; it is used to prioritize renewable-energy technologies or sites.

definition: A fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making method that ranks alternatives by their distances to the fuzzy positive and negative ideal solutions.
comment: Criteria ratings are expressed as fuzzy numbers and alternatives are ranked by closeness coefficient; it is used to select renewable-energy technologies and sites.

definition: A multi-criteria decision-making method that extends VIKOR compromise ranking with fuzzy numbers.
comment: Fuzzy ratings and weights are aggregated into group utility and regret measures to rank alternatives; it is used to select renewable-energy technologies or sites.

definition: Fuzzy WASPAS is a multi-criteria decision-making method that combines the weighted sum and weighted product models under fuzzy evaluations.
comment: Alternatives are scored with fuzzy numbers, the joint generalized criterion aggregates weighted sum and product scores, and the method ranks options such as renewable-energy sites or technologies.

definition: A fuzzy extension of the weighted product multi-criteria decision method in which criteria ratings and weights are expressed as fuzzy numbers.
comment: Alternatives are scored by the product of their fuzzy criteria ratings raised to the criteria weights and then defuzzified for ranking; it is used to compare renewable-energy alternatives.

definition: A multi-criteria decision-making method that aggregates fuzzy criterion scores through a weighted sum.
comment: Fuzzy numbers represent uncertain ratings and weights and alternatives are ranked by their aggregated weighted score; it is used to compare renewable-energy alternatives.

definition: The gamma distribution is a two-parameter continuous probability distribution for positive variables defined by a shape and a scale parameter.
comment: Its flexible right-skewed shape makes it a common alternative to Weibull for fitting wind-speed frequency distributions and for hydrological variables such as rainfall.
distributionParameters: α: shape parameter ; β: scale parameter

definition: A two-component homogeneous mixture distribution formed by the weighted sum of two Gamma distributions.
comment: The mixture captures bimodal or heterogeneous wind regimes better than a single distribution; it is fitted to wind-speed data for wind resource assessment.
distributionParameters: ω: mixing weight ; α_1, α_2: shape parameters ; β_1, β_2: scale parameters

definition: A two-component heterogeneous mixture distribution combining a Gamma distribution and a Gumbel (extreme value type I) distribution.
comment: A mixing weight blends the two component densities to capture bimodal or heterogeneous wind regimes; it is fitted to wind-speed frequency data.
distributionFormula: f(v) = ω v^(α−1) exp(−v/β) / (β^α Γ(α)) + (1−ω)(1/σ) exp[−(v−μ)/σ − exp(−(v−μ)/σ)]
distributionParameters: ω: mixing weight ; α: Gamma shape parameter ; β: Gamma scale parameter ; μ: Gumbel location parameter ; σ: Gumbel scale parameter

definition: The Gamma-inverse Gaussian mixture distribution is a two-component finite mixture probability distribution that combines a Gamma distribution and an inverse Gaussian distribution.
comment: The weighted combination captures bimodal or skewed wind-speed regimes and is compared with other single and mixture laws for wind-speed distribution fitting.
distributionParameters: ω: mixing weight ; α: Gamma shape parameter ; β: Gamma scale parameter ; μ: inverse Gaussian mean parameter ; λ: inverse Gaussian shape parameter

definition: A two-component heterogeneous mixture distribution composed of a Gamma and a Normal probability density.
comment: A mixing weight combines the two components to represent bimodal or asymmetric wind-speed regimes; it is used to fit wind-speed frequency distributions.
distributionParameters: w: mixing weight ; α: Gamma shape parameter ; β: Gamma scale parameter ; μ: Normal mean ; σ: Normal standard deviation

definition: A two-component mixture distribution combining a gamma distribution and a two-parameter Weibull distribution.
comment: The density is a weighted sum of a gamma and a Weibull component, allowing bimodal or irregular wind-speed regimes to be represented in wind resource assessment.
distributionParameters: w: mixing weight ; α: gamma shape parameter ; β: gamma scale parameter ; k: Weibull shape parameter ; c: Weibull scale parameter

definition: A gated recurrent unit network is a recurrent neural network whose cells use update and reset gates to control information flow.
comment: With fewer parameters than LSTM it captures temporal dependencies in sequences; it is used to forecast solar radiation, wind speed and power.

definition: A non-parametric kernel density estimator that uses a Gaussian kernel to estimate a probability density from sample data.
comment: The density is a bandwidth-scaled sum of Gaussian kernels centred on the observations, with the bandwidth chosen by minimising the asymptotic mean integrated squared error; it is used to model wind-speed distributions.
distributionParameters: h: bandwidth ; v_i: sample observations ; n: sample size ; K: Gaussian kernel

definition: A nonparametric estimator of a probability density function that sums Gaussian kernels centred on the observations.
comment: The bandwidth controls smoothness and the estimate makes no assumption about the distribution shape; it is used to model wind-speed and solar-radiation distributions.
distributionParameters: h: bandwidth ; n: sample size ; xi: observations

modelName: Gaussian-kernel fuzzy regression function support vector machine
definition: The Gaussian-kernel FRF-SVM is a support vector machine that uses fuzzy regression functions with a Gaussian kernel to estimate a continuous target.
comment: Combining fuzzy clustering-based regression functions with Gaussian-kernel SVM improves robustness to noisy inputs, and it is used for estimating global solar radiation.

definition: A non-parametric Bayesian regression model that places a Gaussian process prior over functions defined by a mean and a covariance kernel.
comment: Predictions and their uncertainty are obtained from the posterior Gaussian process conditioned on training data; it is used to estimate solar radiation from satellite and meteorological data and to forecast wind power.

definition: A feedforward artificial neural network model in a generalized formulation used for estimating solar radiation components.
comment: It maps meteorological and astronomical inputs to the target through trained hidden layers and is used to estimate daily diffuse solar radiation.

definition: The generalized extreme value distribution is a three-parameter continuous distribution that unifies the Gumbel, Fréchet and Weibull extreme-value families.
comment: It models block maxima and skewed data; in wind studies it is used for extreme and general wind-speed frequency distributions.
distributionFormula: f(x) = (1/σ) t(x)^(ξ+1) exp[−t(x)], with t(x) = [1 + ξ (x − μ)/σ]^(−1/ξ) for ξ ≠ 0
distributionParameters: μ: location parameter ; σ: scale parameter ; ξ: shape parameter

definition: A data-driven fuzzy rule-based model that generalises the Mamdani and Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy models.
comment: Its rules and membership functions are identified from data to represent nonlinear input-output relations; it is used to predict renewable-energy variables, for example after clustering of weather regimes.

definition: The generalized gamma distribution is a three-parameter continuous probability distribution that includes the Weibull, Gamma and exponential distributions as special cases.
comment: Its two shape parameters give more flexibility than the two-parameter Weibull to fit wind-speed frequency distributions.
distributionParameters: a: scale parameter ; b: first shape parameter ; p: second shape parameter

definition: A three-parameter continuous probability distribution with location, scale and shape parameters that generalizes the logistic distribution.
comment: The shape parameter controls skewness, making it able to fit asymmetric data; it is fitted to wind-speed datasets with different characteristics.
distributionFormula: f(x) = α^(−1) e^(−(1−k) y) / (1 + e^(−y))^2, with y = −k^(−1) ln[1 − k (x − ξ)/α] for k ≠ 0 and y = (x − ξ)/α for k = 0
distributionParameters: ξ: location parameter ; α: scale parameter ; k: shape parameter

definition: A three-parameter continuous probability distribution that generalizes the normal distribution and includes lognormal distributions with positive or negative skewness.
comment: A shape parameter controls skewness, the normal law being the case k = 0; it is fitted to wind speed and hydrological data.
distributionFormula: f(x) = exp(k y − y²/2) / (α √(2π)), with y = −(1/k) ln[1 − k (x − ξ)/α] for k ≠ 0 and y = (x − ξ)/α for k = 0
distributionParameters: ξ: location parameter ; α: scale parameter ; k: shape parameter

definition: The generalized Pareto distribution is a continuous distribution for exceedances over a high threshold, defined by location, scale and shape parameters.
comment: It is the limiting distribution of threshold excesses in peaks-over-threshold analysis; it is used to model extreme wind speeds and floods.
distributionParameters: μ: location (threshold) parameter ; σ: scale parameter ; ξ: shape parameter

definition: A continuous lifetime distribution that generalizes the Weibull distribution through an additional power shape parameter.
