comment: The extra shape parameter allows monotone and non-monotone hazard shapes; it is fitted to wind-speed data as an alternative to the Weibull distribution.
distributionParameters: α: shape (α > 0) ; θ: shape (θ > 0) ; λ: scale (λ > 0)

definition: A two-parameter generalisation of the Rayleigh distribution, also known as the Burr type X distribution.
comment: Its shape parameter adds flexibility to the Rayleigh form and its parameters are estimated from data; it is used as a candidate law for wind-speed distributions.
distributionFormula: f(x) = 2 k a² x exp[−(a x)²] {1 − exp[−(a x)²]}^(k−1), x > 0
distributionParameters: a: scale parameter ; k: shape parameter

definition: The genetic approach combining multi-model framework is a hybrid forecasting model that uses genetic-algorithm-based segmentation and clustering of time series with cluster-specific time-delay neural networks.
comment: Series are dynamically segmented by a genetic algorithm, subsequences are clustered into patterns and a dedicated TDNN predicts each pattern, combining the outputs for renewable-energy forecasting.

definition: An evolutionary machine-learning technique that evolves computer programs or symbolic expressions through selection, crossover and mutation.
comment: Candidate expression trees are evolved to minimise prediction error, yielding explicit symbolic models; it is used for symbolic regression of solar radiation and wind variables.

definition: A reservoir operation optimization model for the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam that determines releases and storage.
comment: It optimizes reservoir releases against hydropower generation objectives and downstream penalty terms to study filling and operation strategies.

definition: The GH model is a stochastic generation model that produces synthetic series reproducing the statistical and dynamic features of a benchmarking series.
comment: Parameters are derived from a reference series and used to generate new series with matching statistics and autocorrelation; it is used to synthesize solar-radiation data for simulation.

modelName: global horizontal irradiance autoregressive integrated moving average model
definition: An autoregressive integrated moving average model applied to global horizontal irradiance after seasonal decomposition.
comment: The seasonal component is removed and the residual series is modelled with ARIMA to produce direct GHI forecasts.
timeSeriesModelFormula: φ(B)(1 − B)^d X_t = c + θ(B) ε_t, with φ(B) = 1 − φ1 B − ... − φp B^p and θ(B) = 1 + θ1 B + ... + θq B^q
timeSeriesModelParameters: p: autoregressive order ; d: degree of differencing ; q: moving-average order ; φi: autoregressive coefficients ; θj: moving-average coefficients ; c: constant ; B: backshift operator ; ε_t: white-noise error

definition: A swarm-intelligence metaheuristic in which agents move toward brighter neighbours according to a luciferin level related to fitness.
comment: Agents use adaptive local neighbourhoods, allowing several optima to be found; it is used to determine ensemble weights and tune forecasting models.

definition: The Goodin et al. model is a temperature-based empirical model, a modified Bristow-Campbell form, that estimates daily global solar radiation from the diurnal air-temperature range.
comment: The atmospheric transmittance is expressed as an exponential function of the temperature range normalized by extraterrestrial radiation, with coefficients calibrated locally.
empiricalModelParameters: H: daily global solar radiation ; H0: extraterrestrial radiation ; ΔT: daily maximum minus minimum air temperature ; a, b, c: empirical coefficients
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Used where only air-temperature data are available; requires local calibration

definition: A swarm-intelligence metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the swarming behaviour of grasshoppers.
comment: Search agents move under social attraction and repulsion forces with a decreasing comfort-zone coefficient that balances exploration and exploitation; it is used to tune parameters of predictive models such as ANFIS for renewable-energy forecasting.

modelName: grey wolf optimized least squares support vector machine
definition: A hybrid model in which the hyperparameters of a least squares support vector machine are optimized by the grey wolf optimizer.
comment: The grey wolf metaheuristic searches the regularization and kernel parameters of the LSSVM, improving prediction of variables such as solar radiation or wind power.

modelName: grey wolf optimized support vector regression
definition: GWO-SVR is a hybrid model in which the Grey Wolf Optimizer tunes the hyperparameters of support vector regression.
comment: The metaheuristic searches the penalty and kernel parameters of SVR to minimize prediction error; it is used to forecast solar radiation, wind speed or power.

definition: A hybrid model in which the hyperparameters of an XGBoost gradient boosting model are tuned by the Grey Wolf Optimizer.
comment: The metaheuristic searches the hyperparameter space to minimise prediction error; it is used to predict renewable-energy variables such as solar radiation.

modelName: grid-cell parallel Soil and Water Assessment Tool hydrological model
definition: A grid-cell based, parallelised implementation of the Soil and Water Assessment Tool hydrological model.
comment: It replaces lumped hydrologic response units with spatially explicit grid cells and runs in parallel for large basins; it is used to simulate streamflow and water balance.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Grid-cell parallel implementation of SWAT for watershed water-balance simulation, coupled to a parallel data-assimilation framework.

definition: The Gumbel distribution is a two-parameter extreme-value probability distribution (type I generalized extreme value) for the maximum of a sample.
comment: It is used to fit wind-speed data and especially annual maximum wind speeds and floods for return-level estimation.
distributionParameters: λ: location parameter ; β: scale parameter

definition: A homogeneous two-component mixture distribution combining two Gumbel probability densities.
comment: A mixing weight combines two Gumbel components with distinct location and scale, capturing bimodal wind-speed regimes; it is used to fit wind-speed frequency distributions.
distributionParameters: w: mixing weight ; μ1, μ2: location parameters ; σ1, σ2: scale parameters

definition: A two-component heterogeneous mixture distribution combining a Gumbel (extreme value type I) and a normal distribution.
comment: The weighted sum of a Gumbel and a normal component represents asymmetric or bimodal wind-speed distributions.
distributionParameters: w: mixing weight ; μ1: Gumbel location ; σ1: Gumbel scale ; μ2: normal mean ; σ2: normal standard deviation

modelName: hard-penalty SVM with Glowworm Swarm Optimization
definition: A hard-penalty SVM with Glowworm Swarm Optimization is a hybrid model combining a support vector machine using hard-penalty basis selection with the Glowworm Swarm Optimization metaheuristic for parameter tuning.
comment: The penalty term selects a sparse set of basis functions and the swarm algorithm optimizes the model parameters; it is used for renewable-energy forecasting.

modelName: hard-ridge radial basis function with Cuckoo Search
definition: A hybrid model in which a radial basis function network is pruned with a hard-ridge penalty and optimised by the Cuckoo Search algorithm.
comment: The RBF network is cast as a regression problem whose nodes are pruned and whose parameters are tuned by Cuckoo Search; it is used to predict renewable-energy variables.

modelName: hard-ridge radial basis function with Differential Evolution
definition: A hybrid model in which a radial basis function network regularised by a hard-ridge penalty is optimised by differential evolution.
comment: The penalty prunes hidden nodes and differential evolution tunes the remaining parameters; it is used for renewable-energy prediction tasks such as solar radiation estimation.

definition: The Hargreaves and Samani model is a temperature-based empirical model that estimates daily global solar radiation from extraterrestrial radiation and the square root of the daily air-temperature range.
comment: It assumes the diurnal temperature range reflects cloudiness and atmospheric transmittance, and is widely used where only temperature data are available.
empiricalModelParameters: H: daily global solar radiation ; H0: extraterrestrial radiation ; T_max, T_min: daily maximum and minimum air temperature ; k_r: empirical adjustment coefficient
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Used where only air-temperature data are available; k_r differs between interior and coastal regions

definition: An empirical temperature-based method for estimating reference evapotranspiration from air temperature and extraterrestrial radiation.
comment: It uses the daily temperature range as a proxy for solar radiation; it is used in hydrological models such as SWAT to estimate potential evapotranspiration for water-balance and hydropower studies.
empiricalModelParameters: ET0: reference evapotranspiration (mm/day) ; Ra: extraterrestrial radiation (mm/day equivalent evaporation) ; Tmean: mean daily air temperature (°C) ; Tmax: maximum daily air temperature (°C) ; Tmin: minimum daily air temperature (°C)
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Suitable when only air-temperature data are available; best for periods of five days or longer

modelName: HBV hydrological model with temperature-index snowmelt
definition: A configuration of the HBV conceptual rainfall-runoff model that includes a temperature-index (degree-day) snow routine.
comment: Snow accumulation and melt are computed from air temperature with a degree-day factor, tracking liquid water in the snowpack and snow distribution in grid cells, to simulate runoff for hydropower studies in snow-affected basins.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: HBV conceptual hydrological model with a temperature-index (degree-day) snow accumulation/melt routine.

definition: HEC-GeoHMS river-profile head assessment is a GIS procedure that derives the available hydraulic head of hydropower sites from processed terrain and river profiles.
comment: Elevation drops along river profiles extracted with HEC-GeoHMS are computed and adjusted by the average handheld-GPS error; it is used to estimate gross head for small-hydropower site assessment.

definition: A hydraulic modelling system of the US Army Corps of Engineers that simulates steady and unsteady flow in rivers and open channels.
comment: It solves energy and Saint-Venant equations using channel geometry, discharge and roughness to compute water levels and velocities; it is used in hydropower and flow assessments.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: One-dimensional open-channel hydraulic simulation based on the Saint-Venant continuity and momentum equations.

definition: A satellite-based method that estimates surface global solar irradiance from geostationary satellite imagery through a cloud index and a clear-sky model.
comment: The cloud index derived from observed and reference reflectances is converted into a clear-sky index that scales clear-sky irradiance; it is used to build solar-radiation databases and assess solar resources.
empiricalModelParameters: G: global horizontal irradiance ; Gclear: clear-sky irradiance ; Kc: clear-sky index ; n: cloud index ; ρ: observed apparent albedo ; ρg: ground albedo ; ρc: cloud albedo
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Geostationary satellite visible imagery (e.g. Meteosat)

definition: A hidden Markov model is a statistical model in which an observed sequence is generated by an unobserved Markov chain of hidden states through state-dependent emission distributions.
comment: Parameters are estimated with the Baum-Welch algorithm and hidden states decoded with the Viterbi algorithm; it is used to model regime switching in solar radiation and wind series.

modelName: hidden Markov model Pearson-correlation pattern clustering
definition: A clustering approach that uses a continuous-density hidden Markov model with Pearson correlation as similarity measure to group input sequences by shape.
comment: Sequences are assigned to hidden states or clusters according to correlation-based shape similarity; it is used to extract characteristic weather or irradiance patterns as inputs to forecasting models.

definition: A hierarchical mixture distribution in which each outer component is itself approximated by an inner mixture of distributions.
comment: Outer components such as Weibull, gamma, lognormal and Rayleigh mixtures are weighted and combined to capture complex multimodal wind-speed distributions.
distributionFormula: f(v) = Σ_j π_j Σ_i w_ji f_ji(v; θ_ji)
distributionParameters: π_j: weight of outer component j ; w_ji: weight of inner component i of outer component j ; f_ji: inner component density ; θ_ji: parameters of inner component

definition: A histogram gradient boosting regressor is a gradient-boosted decision-tree ensemble that bins continuous features into histograms to accelerate split finding.
comment: Trees are added sequentially to fit the negative gradient of the loss, using binned features for speed on large datasets; it is used to predict renewable power output and resource variables.

definition: An exponential smoothing time-series model with level, trend and seasonal components.
comment: Each component is updated recursively with smoothing constants and combined to forecast; it is used to predict monthly solar radiation.
timeSeriesModelFormula: ℓ_t = α(y_t − s_(t−m)) + (1 − α)(ℓ_(t−1) + b_(t−1)), b_t = β(ℓ_t − ℓ_(t−1)) + (1 − β) b_(t−1), s_t = γ(y_t − ℓ_t) + (1 − γ) s_(t−m), ŷ_(t+h) = ℓ_t + h b_t + s_(t+h−m) (additive form)
timeSeriesModelParameters: α: level smoothing constant ; β: trend smoothing constant ; γ: seasonal smoothing constant ; m: seasonal period ; ℓ_t: level ; b_t: trend ; s_t: seasonal component

definition: A simulation-based optimisation of microgrid configurations using the HOMER software.
comment: It simulates hourly energy balances over a year for candidate combinations of generators, storage and loads and ranks feasible systems by net present cost; it is used to size hybrid renewable microgrids.

definition: Hunger Games Search is a population-based metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunger-driven foraging behaviour of animals.
comment: Adaptive hunger weights balance exploration and exploitation of candidate solutions; it is used to tune machine learning models and to estimate parameters of renewable-energy systems.

definition: A Weibull-based probability distribution that separately accounts for the frequency of calm (zero) wind speeds.
comment: The probability of calms is treated as a point mass and the non-zero wind speeds follow a two-parameter Weibull law scaled by the non-calm fraction; it is used for wind regimes with a high proportion of calm periods.
distributionParameters: k: shape parameter ; c: scale parameter ; f0: frequency of calm winds

definition: A physical equation that computes theoretical hydropower potential of a river segment from discharge and hydraulic head.
comment: Power is the product of the specific weight of water, the segment average discharge and the head, used to map theoretical hydropower potential along rivers.
physicalModelParameters: P_th: theoretical power ; γ: specific weight of water (ρ g) ; Q: average water discharge ; ΔH: hydraulic head
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Conservation of energy (potential energy of flowing water)

definition: The hydropower equation is a physical model expressing the power obtainable from flowing water as the product of water density, gravity, discharge, head and efficiency.
comment: It converts the gravitational potential energy of falling water into power output; it is the basis of hydropower potential assessment at site and basin scales.
physicalModelFormula: P = ρ g Q H η
physicalModelParameters: P: electrical power ; ρ: water density ; g: gravitational acceleration ; Q: discharge ; H: hydraulic head ; η: overall efficiency
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: conservation of energy (conversion of gravitational potential energy)

definition: An index model adapting the IPAT identity to hydropower as a scaled product of partial population, affluence and technology indices.
comment: It quantifies the combined pressure of population, economic and technological drivers on hydropower development.
empiricalModelParameters: P: partial hydropower population index ; A: partial hydropower affluence index ; T: partial hydropower technology index

definition: A one-dimensional numerical model of water, heat and solute movement in variably saturated porous media.
comment: It solves the Richards equation for soil water flow with root uptake; it is used to estimate soil moisture and infiltration in hydrological studies.

definition: HyperOpt is a hyperparameter optimization method and Python library that performs sequential model-based (Bayesian) optimization, notably with the tree-structured Parzen estimator.
comment: It proposes promising hyperparameter configurations from a probabilistic model of past evaluations; in renewable-energy studies it tunes the hyperparameters of machine learning models such as SVM or CNN-based predictors.

definition: A physical model that computes air density from barometric pressure and absolute air temperature using the ideal gas law.
comment: Density is obtained as pressure divided by the product of the specific gas constant of air and temperature; it is used to correct wind power density and turbine output for local atmospheric conditions.
physicalModelParameters: ρ: air density (kg/m³) ; P: barometric pressure (Pa) ; R: specific gas constant of dry air (287.05 J/(kg·K)) ; T: absolute air temperature (K)
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: ideal gas law

definition: An infinite mixture of Gaussian distributions based on a stick-breaking construction for modelling wind speed.
comment: Component weights follow a Dirichlet-process stick-breaking prior and Gaussian precisions have gamma priors, so the number of components is inferred from the wind-speed data.
distributionFormula: p(x) = Σ(m=1 to M) Δm N(x|μm,σm²)
distributionParameters: Gaussian component weight Δm ; Gaussian mean μm ; Gaussian variance σm² ; Gaussian precision τm ; stick-breaking variable ζm ; Beta-distribution parameter β

definition: IMoG-II is an infinite mixture of Gaussian distributions built with a stick-breaking construction and hierarchical Gamma priors for modelling wind-speed distributions.
comment: Component weights are generated by a stick-breaking process and Gaussian precisions receive Gamma priors so the effective number of components is inferred from data; it is used for flexible nonparametric-Bayesian wind-speed density estimation.
distributionFormula: p(x) = Σ(m=1 to M) Δm N(x|μm,σm²)
distributionParameters: Gaussian component weight Δm ; Gaussian mean μm ; Gaussian variance σm² ; Gaussian precision τm ; stick-breaking variable ζm ; Beta-distribution parameter β

definition: A metaheuristic optimisation algorithm that enhances Atom Search Optimization with piecewise linear chaotic map initialisation and Lévy flight.
comment: The improvements increase population diversity and escape from local optima; it is used to optimise an outlier-robust extreme learning machine for renewable-energy prediction.

modelName: improved grey wolf optimized least squares support vector machine
definition: A hybrid model in which the hyperparameters of a least squares support vector machine are optimised by an improved grey wolf optimiser.
comment: The improved optimiser uses a nonlinear convergence factor to search kernel width and regularisation values; it is used to forecast wind speed, solar radiation or power output.

definition: The improved multilayer neural network is a feedforward neural network with several hidden layers enhanced by ReLU activation, L2 regularization, Adam optimization and adaptive inverse normalization.
comment: These training refinements reduce overfitting and speed up convergence when predicting continuous renewable-energy variables.

definition: A maximum power point tracking algorithm for photovoltaic systems that compares the incremental and instantaneous conductance of the array.
comment: Since dP/dV = 0 at the maximum power point, the operating voltage is adjusted until dI/dV equals −I/V; it improves on perturb-and-observe under rapidly changing irradiance.

definition: A set of hydrologic statistics that quantify streamflow regime changes in magnitude, timing, frequency, duration and rate of change.
comment: Pre- and post-impact flow records are compared using IHA and environmental flow component parameters grouped in ecologically relevant groups, to assess the impacts of dams and hydropower operation.

definition: The Indus Waters Treaty is a 1960 bilateral water-sharing treaty between India and Pakistan governing the use of the Indus river system.
comment: It allocates the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) mainly to Pakistan and constrains Indian run-of-river hydropower design, notably in Jammu and Kashmir.

definition: A theory explaining how innovations spread through a social system as a function of their perceived attributes and communication channels.
comment: Adoption depends on relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability and observability; it is used to analyse barriers to renewable-energy technology adoption.

definition: A coordinated planning approach for renewable electricity across the European Union that aligns national and European scenarios.
comment: It combines scenarios for demand, renewable deployment, grids, storage and flexibility to guide policy; it is a planning and policy approach rather than a model.

definition: Inverse distance weighting is a deterministic spatial interpolation method that estimates values at unsampled locations as a weighted average of nearby observations with weights inversely proportional to a power of distance.
comment: It is used in GIS-based renewable-energy studies to interpolate station measurements or suitability values into continuous maps.

definition: A two-parameter continuous probability distribution of the reciprocal of a Gamma-distributed variable.
comment: Its right-skewed, heavy-tailed density is fitted to positive data; it is used to model wind-speed distributions and derive wind power density.
distributionParameters: p: shape parameter ; b: scale parameter

definition: A two-parameter continuous probability distribution for positive variables, also called the Wald distribution.
comment: Defined by a mean and a shape parameter, it is fitted to wind speed frequency distributions as an alternative to the Weibull law.
distributionParameters: μ: mean parameter ; λ: shape parameter

definition: The inverse Weibull distribution is a two-parameter continuous distribution of a variable whose reciprocal follows a Weibull distribution.
comment: Its heavier right tail and unimodal shape make it an alternative to Weibull for fitting wind-speed frequency distributions.
distributionParameters: a: shape parameter ; b: scale parameter

definition: A three-parameter continuous distribution obtained by inverting a Kumaraswamy random variable, with one scale and two shape parameters.
comment: It has a heavy right tail suited to positive skewed data; it is fitted to wind-speed data for wind resource assessment.
distributionParameters: α: shape parameter ; β: shape parameter ; σ: scale parameter

definition: A gridded annual water-balance model of the InVEST suite that estimates water yield from precipitation and evapotranspiration.
comment: It uses the Budyko framework with land cover, soil depth and plant-available water to compute yield per pixel; it is used to assess water supply for hydropower and ecosystem services.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: InVEST annual water-yield model links annual precipitation and evapotranspiration through a Budyko-type water-balance framework to estimate watershed water yield.

definition: The Iqbal model is an empirical model attributed to Iqbal for estimating diffuse solar radiation from global radiation through correlations with the clearness index or sunshine fraction.
comment: It serves as a benchmark for other diffuse-fraction correlations when diffuse radiation measurements are unavailable.
empiricalModelParameters: H_d: diffuse solar radiation [MJ m^-2 d^-1]; H_g: global solar radiation [MJ m^-2 d^-1]; H_0: extraterrestrial radiation [MJ m^-2 d^-1]; S: sunshine duration [h]; S_0: maximum possible sunshine duration [h]

definition: A bounded four-parameter continuous probability distribution obtained by a logit-type transformation of a normal variable, also known as the four-parameter lognormal distribution.
comment: Two shape parameters, a location and a range parameter allow it to fit bounded data with diverse skewness and kurtosis; it is used to model wind-speed distributions.
distributionFormula: f(x) = δ λ / [√(2π) (x − ξ)(ξ + λ − x)] · exp{−½ [γ + δ ln((x − ξ)/(ξ + λ − x))]^2}, ξ < x < ξ + λ
distributionParameters: γ: first shape parameter ; δ: second shape parameter ; ξ: location parameter ; λ: scale (range) parameter

definition: A bivariate angular-linear distribution constructed by the Johnson-Wehrly method for the joint description of a linear and a circular variable.
comment: The specified marginals of wind speed and wind direction are linked through a circular density of a dependence variable; it is used to model joint wind speed and direction for wind resource assessment.
distributionFormula: f(v,θ) = 2π g(ζ) f_V(v) f_Θ(θ), with ζ = 2π[F_V(v) − F_Θ(θ)]
distributionParameters: f_V, F_V: marginal pdf and cdf of wind speed ; f_Θ, F_Θ: marginal pdf and cdf of wind direction ; g: circular density of the dependence variable ζ

modelName: Jones and Underwood photovoltaic thermal model
definition: The Jones and Underwood model is a lumped-capacitance energy-balance model of photovoltaic module temperature.
comment: It balances absorbed shortwave irradiance, longwave radiative exchange, convective heat loss and electrical output against the module heat capacity; it is used to predict transient PV cell temperature and its effect on power.
physicalModelFormula: C dTm/dt = α A G + ε σ A (Tsky⁴ − Tm⁴) − h_c A (Tm − Ta) − P
physicalModelParameters: C: module heat capacity ; Tm: module temperature ; α: absorptivity ; A: module area ; G: irradiance ; ε: emissivity ; σ: Stefan–Boltzmann constant ; Tsky: sky temperature ; h_c: convective heat-transfer coefficient ; Ta: ambient temperature ; P: electrical power output
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: conservation of energy (transient heat balance)

definition: An empirical model by Justus and Mikhail that extrapolates Weibull shape and scale parameters from a reference height to another height.
comment: The scale parameter follows a power law whose exponent depends on the reference scale, and the shape parameter is adjusted logarithmically with height; it is used to estimate hub-height wind distributions.
empiricalModelParameters: c_a, k_a: Weibull scale and shape at reference height z_a ; c(z), k(z): Weibull scale and shape at height z ; n: power-law exponent ; z_a: reference height (m)
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: heights in metres, c in m/s, neutral stability, lower atmospheric boundary layer

definition: An empirical method that extrapolates Weibull scale and shape parameters of wind speed from the measurement height to another height.
comment: It applies a power-law to the scale parameter with an exponent depending on the reference scale parameter and a logarithmic correction to the shape parameter; it is used to estimate wind resources at hub height.
empiricalModelParameters: c(h): scale parameter at height h ; k(h): shape parameter at height h ; c0: scale parameter at reference height ; k0: shape parameter at reference height ; h: target height (m) ; h0: reference height (m) ; n: power-law exponent
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Neutral stability, flat terrain, reference height near 10 m

definition: K-means solar-radiation zoning is the application of the k-means clustering algorithm to partition stations or grid cells into zones with similar solar-radiation characteristics.
comment: Observations are iteratively assigned to the nearest of k centroids and centroids recomputed to minimize within-cluster variance, yielding homogeneous solar-radiation zones for resource assessment.

definition: A maximum power point tracking algorithm for photovoltaic systems that uses a Kalman filter to estimate the voltage of the maximum power point.
comment: The Kalman filter recursively estimates the optimal operating point from noisy voltage, current and power measurements, giving fast and stable tracking under varying irradiance.

modelName: Kalman filter - multiple regression hybrid model
definition: A hybrid nowcasting model that fuses Kalman-filter and multiple-regression predictions.
comment: The two predictions are combined with weights based on their local root mean square errors, for short-term solar or wind nowcasting.

modelName: Kalman photovoltaic power prediction based on forecasting experience
definition: A Kalman-filter photovoltaic power prediction model that uses a fitted dynamic equation built from past forecasting experience to correct PV power forecasts.
comment: The state equation is fitted from historical NWP and photoelectric forecast errors and the filter updates predictions with measured power; it is used for short-term PV power forecasting.

definition: A model-free filtering method that combines the Kalman filter with Takens delay-coordinate embedding to forecast system states from past observations.
comment: The dynamics are replaced by a local proxy built from nearest neighbours in the reconstructed delay space, and the Kalman update corrects the forecast; it is used to forecast solar or wind time series.
timeSeriesModelParameters: d: embedding dimension ; τ: time delay ; number of nearest neighbours ; Q, R: process and observation noise covariances

definition: An empirical model that estimates solar irradiance as a function of the day of the year.
comment: It represents the seasonal variation of daily irradiance with a periodic function of the day number fitted to local data; it is used to estimate solar radiation where measurements are scarce.
empiricalModelParameters: G(t): irradiance at hour t [W m^-2]; t: hour of day; a,b: parameters determined from boundary conditions and average daily irradiance

definition: The four-parameter Kappa distribution is a continuous probability distribution that includes the generalized logistic, generalized extreme value and generalized Pareto distributions as special cases.
comment: Its two shape parameters give high flexibility for fitting wind-speed and hydrological data, typically estimated by L-moments or maximum likelihood.
distributionParameters: ξ: location parameter ; α: scale parameter ; k: first shape parameter ; h: second shape parameter

definition: A three-dimensional non-hydrostatic atmospheric mesoscale model developed at Karlsruhe for simulating regional wind and flow fields.
comment: It solves the atmospheric equations of motion over complex terrain to compute three-dimensional wind vectors on a regional grid; it is used to map wind resources over national or regional areas.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Three-dimensional atmospheric mesoscale numerical model used to calculate wind vectors over the study area.

definition: A non-parametric method that estimates a probability density function as the average of kernel functions centred on the observations.
comment: The smoothness of the estimate is controlled by the bandwidth and no distribution shape is assumed; it is used to model wind speed distributions with irregular or multimodal shapes.
distributionParameters: K: kernel function ; h: bandwidth ; n: sample size ; v_i: observations

definition: Kernel nearest neighbor is an instance-based learning model that predicts from the k nearest training samples weighted by a kernel function of distance.
comment: Closer neighbours receive larger weights in the prediction; it is used to estimate solar radiation or renewable output, here with region-specific k.

definition: A procedure by Klein that selects a recommended average day for each month to represent monthly mean extraterrestrial and solar-geometry quantities.
comment: The representative day numbers are used to compute declination and extraterrestrial radiation in monthly solar radiation estimation.

definition: A feature-selection procedure based on the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression.
comment: The L1 penalty shrinks some coefficients to zero so that only informative predictors remain, with the penalty chosen by cross-validation; it is used to select inputs for renewable-energy forecasting models.

definition: Lasso regression is a linear regression method that adds an L1 penalty on coefficients to perform simultaneous regularization and variable selection.
comment: Coefficients of uninformative predictors are shrunk to zero; it is used for feature selection and for estimating variables such as wind speed at hub height from meteorological predictors.

definition: A linear regression model with forward stepwise selection of predictors, as implemented by the leapForward method.
comment: Predictors are added one at a time according to their improvement of the fit and the subset size is chosen by resampling; it is used as a forecasting benchmark for solar radiation.

definition: A gradient boosting ensemble that sequentially fits regression trees to the residuals under a squared-error loss.
comment: Each weak regression tree is fitted to the current residuals and added with a learning rate; it is used to predict solar radiation, wind power and other continuous renewable-energy variables.

definition: The least squares support vector machine is a variant of the support vector machine that replaces inequality constraints with equality constraints and a squared-error loss, solved by a linear system.
comment: With a kernel such as the Gaussian RBF it performs nonlinear regression efficiently; it is used to predict solar radiation, wind speed and power.

definition: A second-order training algorithm for neural networks that minimises a sum of squared errors by interpolating between Gauss–Newton and gradient descent.
comment: A damping parameter is adjusted at each iteration to balance speed and stability; it is used to train ANNs predicting renewable-energy variables.

definition: A methodology that quantifies the environmental burdens of a product or power plant over its whole life cycle.
comment: It inventories material and energy flows from construction to decommissioning and converts them into impact indicators; it is used to compare the environmental performance of energy technologies and is a method rather than a model.

definition: The Light Gradient Boosting Machine is a gradient-boosted decision-tree framework that uses histogram-based leaf-wise tree growth with gradient-based one-side sampling and exclusive feature bundling.
comment: These techniques speed up training on large datasets while preserving accuracy; it is used to predict solar radiation, wind power and other renewable-energy variables.

definition: A statistical model that expresses a response variable as a linear function of one or more predictors plus an error term.
comment: Coefficients are estimated by ordinary least squares; in renewable-energy studies it is used to relate solar radiation, wind speed, Weibull parameters or energy output to explanatory variables.

definition: A bias-correction method that adjusts climate model outputs by the difference or ratio between observed and simulated means.
comment: Additive corrections are applied to variables such as temperature and multiplicative corrections to precipitation, used to correct climate model data before hydrological or renewable-energy impact studies.
empiricalModelFormula: x_corr = x_mod + (μ_obs − μ_mod) (additive) ; x_corr = x_mod × (μ_obs / μ_mod) (multiplicative)
empiricalModelParameters: x_mod: model output ; x_corr: corrected value ; μ_obs: mean of observations ; μ_mod: mean of model output over the reference period
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Corrects the mean only, typically monthly; assumes stationary bias

definition: A linear semivariogram is a geostatistical model in which semivariance increases linearly with separation distance, optionally with a nugget.
comment: It describes spatial correlation for kriging interpolation; it is used to map wind, solar or hydrological variables from station data.

definition: An isotropic sky model by Liu and Jordan that converts horizontal beam and diffuse radiation into total radiation on a tilted surface.
comment: Beam radiation is projected geometrically, sky diffuse is assumed isotropic and ground-reflected radiation depends on albedo; it is used to estimate irradiation on inclined PV and collector surfaces.
empiricalModelFormula: H_T = H_b R_b + H_d (1 + cos β)/2 + H ρ_g (1 − cos β)/2
empiricalModelParameters: H_T: radiation on tilted surface ; H: global horizontal radiation ; H_b: beam horizontal radiation ; H_d: diffuse horizontal radiation ; R_b: beam tilt factor ; β: surface tilt angle ; ρ_g: ground albedo
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: isotropic diffuse sky assumption

definition: An ensemble Kalman filter variant that performs the analysis locally in the ensemble space using a transform of the ensemble perturbations.
comment: Localisation allows efficient parallel assimilation of observations into high-dimensional models; it is used to assimilate observations into numerical models such as solar-wind or weather models.

definition: The log-logistic distribution is a two-parameter continuous probability distribution of a positive variable whose logarithm follows a logistic distribution.
comment: It is fitted to wind-speed frequency distributions as an alternative to the Weibull distribution.
distributionParameters: α: scale parameter ; β: shape parameter

definition: A three-parameter continuous probability distribution in which the logarithm of the variable follows a Pearson type III distribution.
comment: Data are log-transformed and fitted with a shifted Gamma (Pearson type III) law; it is used in flood-frequency analysis and to model wind-speed distributions.
distributionParameters: α: shape parameter ; β: scale parameter ; ξ: location parameter

modelName: log-transformed autoregressive integrated moving average with time-varying coefficients
definition: An ARIMA model fitted to the logarithm of a series with coefficients allowed to vary over time.
comment: The log transform stabilizes variance and the time-varying coefficients follow changing dynamics; it is used to forecast solar radiation.
timeSeriesModelFormula: φ_t(B)(1 − B)^d ln y_t = c + θ_t(B) ε_t
timeSeriesModelParameters: p: autoregressive order ; d: degree of differencing ; q: moving-average order ; φ_(i,t): time-varying autoregressive coefficients ; θ_(j,t): time-varying moving-average coefficients ; ε_t: white-noise error ; B: backshift operator

definition: The logarithmic wind profile law is a model describing the increase of mean wind speed with height in the atmospheric surface layer as a logarithmic function of height over the roughness length.
comment: It is used to extrapolate measured wind speeds to turbine hub height in wind resource assessment.
empiricalModelParameters: U(z): wind speed at height z ; U(zr): wind speed at reference height zr ; z0: surface roughness length
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: neutral atmospheric stability; surface layer over homogeneous terrain

definition: An empirical logarithmic wind profile that relates wind speeds at two heights through the surface roughness length.
comment: Wind speed is assumed to increase with the logarithm of height above the roughness length; it is used to extrapolate measured wind speeds to turbine hub height.
empiricalModelParameters: v1: wind speed at height h1 ; v2: wind speed at height h2 ; z0: surface roughness length
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: neutral atmospheric stability, surface layer, homogeneous terrain

definition: A two-parameter symmetric continuous probability distribution whose cumulative distribution function is the logistic function.
comment: Its location and scale parameters are fitted to data; it is evaluated as a candidate law for wind-speed distributions.
distributionParameters: μ: location parameter ; s: scale parameter

modelName: logistic-sigmoid artificial neural network with 50 hidden neurons
definition: The logistic-sigmoid artificial neural network with 50 hidden neurons is a feedforward neural network with one hidden layer of 50 neurons using logistic sigmoid activation.
comment: It is trained by backpropagation to map meteorological inputs to a continuous renewable-energy target as one of several compared ANN configurations.

definition: An S-shaped growth model that describes the cumulative diffusion of a technology toward a finite saturation level.
comment: Cumulative installed capacity grows slowly, accelerates and then saturates at the technical potential; it is used to project the deployment of renewable-energy technologies.
empiricalModelParameters: C(t): cumulative installed capacity at time t ; K: saturation level (technical potential) ; r: growth rate ; t0: inflection time

definition: A two-parameter continuous probability distribution of a positive variable whose logarithm is normally distributed.
comment: Its density is defined by the mean and standard deviation of the log variable; it is widely fitted to wind speed frequency distributions and compared with the Weibull law.
distributionParameters: μ: mean of ln(v) ; σ: standard deviation of ln(v)

definition: A long short-term memory network is a recurrent neural network whose memory cells use input, forget and output gates to retain long-term dependencies.
comment: The gating mitigates vanishing gradients in sequence learning; it is widely used to forecast wind speed, solar irradiance, streamflow and renewable power.

modelName: long short-term memory solar irradiation and temperature model
definition: A long short-term memory recurrent neural network that jointly forecasts 24-hour solar irradiation and air temperature.
comment: Gated memory cells capture temporal dependencies in meteorological sequences; it is used for day-ahead solar resource forecasting.

definition: A decision-tree learning algorithm whose leaves contain multivariate linear regression models.
comment: The tree splits the input space to reduce standard deviation and fits linear models at the leaves, followed by pruning and smoothing; it is used to forecast solar radiation, streamflow and wind variables.

definition: The marching-squares algorithm is a computer-graphics procedure that extracts contour lines from a two-dimensional scalar grid.
comment: Each grid cell is classified by which corners lie above the contour level and line segments are drawn by lookup and interpolation; it is used to convert gridded forecasts into contour maps rather than to model a phenomenon.

definition: A nature-inspired metaheuristic optimization algorithm based on the foraging strategies of marine predators using Lévy and Brownian movements.
comment: The search switches between exploration and exploitation phases following the optimal encounter-rate policy of predators and prey; it is used for feature selection and parameter tuning of renewable-energy prediction models.

definition: A Gaussian process regression model using the Matérn covariance kernel with smoothness parameter 5/2.
comment: It places a Gaussian process prior over functions and gives predictions with uncertainty from the posterior; it is used for non-parametric prediction of solar radiation and wind power.

modelName: Max Planck Institute Earth System Model
definition: The Max Planck Institute Earth System Model is a coupled global Earth-system model combining the ECHAM atmosphere, MPIOM ocean and JSBACH land components.
comment: Its simulations contribute to CMIP5 and CMIP6; projections are used to assess climate-change impacts on renewable-energy resources such as hydropower and wind.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Earth-system model with atmospheric/ocean/land components used for climate projections.

definition: A nonlinear programming model that estimates maximum-entropy probability density parameters by maximising Shannon entropy under normalisation and moment constraints.
comment: Parameters are obtained by numerically minimising a cost function of relative errors in the constraints; it is used to derive maximum-entropy wind-speed distributions.

definition: A probability density function obtained by maximising Shannon entropy subject to constraints on the moments of the data.
comment: The Lagrange multipliers are solved so that the distribution reproduces the sample moments; it is used to model wind-speed distributions with flexible shapes.
distributionParameters: λi: Lagrange multipliers ; N: number of moment constraints

definition: The maximum extractable wind-energy equation is a physical model that gives the upper bound of energy a turbine can extract from a wind stream, equal to the Betz fraction of the kinetic energy flux.
comment: It multiplies the kinetic energy available in the wind by the Betz limit of 16/27 and is used to estimate the theoretical maximum wind energy at a site.
physicalModelParameters: E_max: maximum extractable energy ; ρ: air density ; A: rotor swept area ; v: wind speed ; t: time duration ; 16/27: Betz limit
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Kinetic energy flux and actuator-disc momentum theory (Betz limit)

definition: A statistical method that estimates the long-term wind climate at a target site by correlating short-term on-site measurements with concurrent long-term reference data.
comment: A relationship fitted over the concurrent period, typically linear, is applied to the long-term reference record to predict long-term wind speeds at the target site; it is used in wind resource assessment.
empiricalModelParameters: V̂: predicted wind speed at the target site ; U: wind speed at the reference site ; a: slope ; b: intercept
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Requires a concurrent measurement period and good correlation between target and reference sites

definition: A study-specific group of hybrid empirical models that estimate solar radiation from combinations of meteorological predictors.
comment: The models combine several meteorological variables in empirical regression equations and were compared with other model groups in the study.

definition: The micro-hydropower potential power equation is a physical model computing the power available at a micro-hydropower site from head and dependable discharge.
comment: It applies the hydropower equation to the design (dependable) discharge and available head; it is used to size micro-hydropower schemes.
physicalModelFormula: P = ρ g Q H η
physicalModelParameters: P: power ; ρ: water density ; g: gravitational acceleration ; Q: dependable discharge ; H: available head ; η: overall efficiency
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: conservation of energy (conversion of gravitational potential energy)

definition: A data preprocessing step that linearly rescales each variable to a fixed interval using its minimum and maximum values.
comment: It puts input variables on a common scale before training machine learning models for renewable-energy prediction.

definition: A mathematical optimisation model with a linear objective and linear constraints in which some decision variables are restricted to integers.
comment: Binary variables represent on/off states and discrete choices while continuous variables represent flows; it is used for scheduling and sizing renewable-energy and storage systems.

definition: The mixture kernel density model is a probability density model formed as a weighted sum of several kernel density estimators.
comment: Each component kernel density has its own bandwidth and weight coefficient summing to one, providing a flexible nonparametric representation of multimodal wind-speed or power distributions.
distributionFormula: f_MKD(x) = Σ(j=1 to M) a_j f_j(x); Σ(j=1 to M) a_j = 1.
distributionParameters: weight coefficients a_j ; bandwidths h_j ; number of mixture kernel densities M

definition: A finite mixture probability distribution composed of weighted lognormal component densities.
comment: Each component captures a distinct mode of the data and weights sum to one; it is used to fit multimodal wind-speed distributions.
distributionFormula: f(v) = Σ(i=1 to m) wi · (1/(v σi √(2π))) exp[−(ln v − μi)^2 / (2σi^2)], Σ wi = 1
distributionParameters: wi: mixing weight of component i ; μi: log-mean of component i ; σi: log-standard deviation of component i ; m: number of components

definition: A finite mixture distribution formed by a weighted sum of Rayleigh distributions.
comment: Each Rayleigh component has its own scale parameter, allowing multimodal wind-speed distributions to be represented.
distributionFormula: f(v) = Σ_(i=1..M) w_i (v/σ_i²) exp[−v²/(2σ_i²)], with Σ w_i = 1
distributionParameters: w_i: weight of component i ; σ_i: scale parameter of component i ; M: number of components

modelName: Monte Carlo annual energy production simulation
definition: A stochastic simulation model that estimates annual energy production by repeated random sampling of wind conditions through a turbine power curve.
comment: Crude Monte Carlo sampling propagates wind-speed variability and uncertainty to produce a distribution of annual energy production.

definition: A recurrent neural network trained and applied over a moving window of recent observations.
comment: The window is shifted as new data arrive so that the network adapts to recent dynamics; it is used for short-term forecasting of renewable-energy time series.

definition: A multi-output multilayer perceptron is a feedforward neural network with several output neurons that predicts multiple targets simultaneously.
comment: It forecasts, for example, the 24 hourly solar irradiation values of the next day in one pass from endogenous and exogenous inputs.

definition: A distribution model expressed as a sum of Gaussian functions fitted to the observed wind-speed frequency distribution.
comment: Each Gaussian peak has its own amplitude, centre and width, allowing multimodal frequency distributions to be represented; it is used to describe wind-speed frequency at sites with several wind regimes.
distributionFormula: y = f(x) = Σ(i = 1 to n) Ai exp[−(x−xi)^2/(2si^2)]
distributionParameters: Ai ; xi ; si

definition: An institutional platform for dialogue, knowledge sharing and coordinated action among renewable-energy stakeholder groups.
comment: It supports participatory renewable-energy planning; it is an organizational arrangement rather than a model.

definition: A multilayer perceptron is a feedforward artificial neural network with one or more hidden layers of nonlinear neurons fully connected between layers.
comment: Trained by backpropagation, it learns nonlinear input-output mappings; it is widely used to predict solar radiation, wind speed and power and renewable-energy outputs.

modelName: multilayer perceptron - Gaussian process regression hybrid model
definition: A hybrid model in which multilayer perceptron outputs are fed into Gaussian process regression.
comment: The MLP captures nonlinear structure and the GPR yields predictions with uncertainty intervals; it is used for probabilistic renewable-energy prediction.

definition: A statistical model that expresses a dependent variable as a linear combination of several independent variables plus an error term.
comment: Coefficients are estimated by least squares; it is used to relate renewable power generation or solar radiation to meteorological variables.

definition: The multiple regressor nowcaster is a multiple regression model that predicts near-term solar irradiance from recent irradiance history and features extracted from all-sky images.
comment: Cloud features from sky cameras and past measurements are combined linearly to produce intra-hour irradiance nowcasts for solar power plants.

definition: A non-parametric regression model that builds a piecewise-linear function from adaptively selected hinge basis functions and their interactions.
comment: Basis functions are added in a forward pass and pruned in a backward pass by generalized cross-validation; it is used to forecast solar radiation and wind power.

definition: A smooth multivariate wind distribution model based on multivariate kernel density estimation of wind speed, wind direction and air density.
comment: It captures coupled variation of the variables without assuming unimodality, for more accurate wind resource and power assessment.
distributionParameters: Bandwidth h for univariate KDE and bandwidth matrix H for multivariate KDE.

definition: A naive Bayes GHI classifier is a probabilistic classifier that assigns global horizontal irradiance classes using Bayes theorem under conditional independence of features.
comment: Class probabilities are computed from weather-forecast and diurnal features; it is used to categorize solar-irradiance conditions for forecasting.

definition: A two-parameter continuous distribution related to the Gamma distribution, also called the Nakagami-m distribution.
comment: It is defined by a shape and a spread parameter and reduces to the Rayleigh distribution for m = 1; it is fitted to wind-speed data for wind resource assessment.
distributionFormula: f(x) = [2 m^m / (Γ(m) Ω^m)] x^(2m−1) exp(−m x²/Ω), x ≥ 0
distributionParameters: m: shape parameter ; Ω: spread parameter

definition: A conceptual flow-routing model that represents a catchment response as a series of identical linear reservoirs.
comment: Inflow passes through the reservoir cascade, producing a gamma-shaped unit hydrograph; it is used to route runoff in rainfall-runoff models.

definition: The Nash model is a conceptual hydrological routing model that represents a catchment as a cascade of identical linear reservoirs.
comment: Its instantaneous unit hydrograph follows a gamma function defined by the number of reservoirs and their storage constant, and it routes simulated runoff to obtain discharge for hydropower assessment.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Hydrological flow routing using a Nash-type cascade/routing formulation with locally calibrated parameters.

definition: A conceptual framework that analyses innovation as the outcome of interactions among actors, institutions and knowledge flows within a national system.
comment: It examines firms, research organisations, policies, market transactions and incentives to explain technology development; it is used to study the diffusion of renewable-energy technologies.

definition: A hydraulic equation that computes the net head available to a hydropower turbine from gross head and head losses.
comment: Net head is obtained by subtracting conduit head losses (and accounting for maximum tailwater level) from the gross head, and is used to calculate hydropower output.
physicalModelParameters: H_n: net head ; H_g: gross head ; h_L: head losses in conduits
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Conservation of energy (Bernoulli equation)

modelName: nominal operating cell temperature thermal model
definition: The NOCT thermal model is an empirical model estimating photovoltaic cell temperature from ambient temperature, irradiance and the nominal operating cell temperature.
comment: Cell temperature rises linearly with irradiance scaled by the NOCT test conditions; it is used to correct PV efficiency and power for temperature.
empiricalModelParameters: Tc: cell temperature (°C) ; Ta: ambient temperature (°C) ; NOCT: nominal operating cell temperature (°C) ; G: irradiance (W/m²)
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: steady state, conditions close to NOCT test (low wind speed, open-rack mounting)

definition: A wind-speed distribution derived from superstatistics in which Gaussian wind components have fluctuating variance whose inverse follows a Gamma distribution.
comment: Integrating over the fluctuating parameter gives a non-Gaussian distribution of wind speed; it is fitted to wind-speed data as an alternative to the Weibull distribution.
distributionParameters: b ; c

definition: A multi-objective metaheuristic that combines the bat algorithm with nondominated sorting to approximate a Pareto front.
comment: Bats adjust frequency, loudness and pulse rate while nondominated sorting ranks solutions; it is used to optimise ensemble forecasting weights for accuracy and stability.

definition: The normal distribution is a two-parameter symmetric continuous probability distribution defined by its mean and standard deviation.
comment: It is used as a reference law for wind-speed and other meteorological variables, although it fits skewed wind-speed data less well than Weibull-type laws.
distributionParameters: μ: mean (location parameter) ; σ: standard deviation (scale parameter)

definition: A two-component mixture of singly truncated normal distributions defined on non-negative values.
comment: Each component is a normal density truncated at zero and renormalized, and a weight combines them to fit bimodal wind regimes; it is used to model wind-speed frequency distributions.
distributionParameters: w: mixing weight ; l1, l2: location (mean) parameters ; r1, r2: scale (standard deviation) parameters ; Φ: standard normal cumulative distribution function

definition: A two-component mixture distribution of a singly truncated normal distribution and a two-parameter Weibull distribution.
comment: The truncated normal component accounts for a mode of wind speeds while the Weibull component describes the rest, improving fit for bimodal wind regimes.
distributionFormula: f(v) = w [1/(I₀ σ √(2π))] exp[−(v − μ)²/(2σ²)] + (1 − w) (k/c)(v/c)^(k−1) exp[−(v/c)^k], with I₀ = Φ(μ/σ)
distributionParameters: w: mixing weight ; μ: normal mean ; σ: normal standard deviation ; k: Weibull shape parameter ; c: Weibull scale parameter ; I₀: truncation normalizing factor

definition: An NSMOBA-optimized ANN ensemble is a hybrid model combining several artificial neural networks whose combination weights are optimized by a nondominated-sorting multiobjective bat algorithm.
comment: The multiobjective metaheuristic balances accuracy and stability criteria when weighting member forecasts; it is used for wind speed or power forecasting.

definition: A single-hidden-layer extreme learning machine whose hidden neurons are ranked by multiresponse sparse regression and pruned by leave-one-out cross-validation.
comment: Hidden weights are random and output weights are solved analytically, with pruning improving robustness; it is used to forecast renewable-energy time series.

definition: A multilayer perceptron with an optimised architecture and parameters that uses several input variables.
comment: The network maps preprocessed multivariate meteorological inputs to the target through hidden layers; it is used to predict daily solar radiation.

definition: The outlier-robust extreme learning machine is a single-hidden-layer feedforward neural network trained as an extreme learning machine with a loss formulation robust to outliers.
comment: Hidden weights are random and output weights are solved with an L1-norm based robust objective, which reduces the influence of anomalous training data in renewable-energy prediction.

definition: A kernel density estimator whose bandwidth is selected by the oversmoothed cross-validation criterion.
comment: The density is estimated as an average of kernels centred on each observation, with the bandwidth chosen to balance bias and variance; it is used to estimate wind-speed distributions without assuming a parametric form.
distributionFormula: f̂(v) = (1/(n h)) Σ(i=1 to n) K((v − v_i)/h)
distributionParameters: h: bandwidth (smoothing parameter) ; K: kernel function ; n: sample size ; v_i: observed values

definition: A parabolic (quadratic) approximation of the wind-turbine power curve defined by cut-in, rated and cut-off wind speeds and rated power.
comment: Power rises quadratically between cut-in and rated speed, stays at rated power up to cut-off and is zero elsewhere; it is used to estimate turbine energy yield from wind speed distributions.
empiricalModelFormula: P(v) = PeR (v² − vc²)/(vR² − vc²) for vc ≤ v < vR ; P(v) = PeR for vR ≤ v ≤ vF ; P(v) = 0 for v < vc or v > vF
empiricalModelParameters: vc: cut-in wind speed ; vR: rated wind speed ; vF: cut-off wind speed ; PeR: rated electrical power
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: When manufacturer power-curve data are unavailable

definition: ParaSol is a parameter-optimization and uncertainty-analysis method based on the shuffled complex evolution algorithm, used for calibrating hydrological models.
comment: It minimizes an objective function of simulated versus observed flows and derives parameter uncertainty ranges; it is used to calibrate SWAT parameters in hydropower-related hydrological studies.

definition: A population-based metaheuristic optimisation algorithm in which candidate solutions move through the search space guided by their own and the swarm best positions.
comment: PSO updates particle velocities iteratively; it is used to tune machine learning hyperparameters such as SVR parameters and to size renewable systems.

modelName: particle swarm optimized least squares support vector machine
definition: A hybrid model in which the hyperparameters of a least squares support vector machine are optimised by particle swarm optimisation.
comment: The swarm searches the kernel and regularisation parameters to minimise prediction error; it is used to forecast wind speed, solar radiation and power output.

definition: The Parton and Logan model is an empirical model that estimates the diurnal course of air temperature from daily maximum and minimum temperatures.
comment: It uses a truncated sine function during daylight and an exponential decay at night, and is used to generate hourly temperature series for solar and energy applications.
empiricalModelFormula: Day: T = T_min + (T_max − T_min) sin[π m / (Y + 2a)] ; Night: T = T_min + (T_sn − T_min) exp(−b n / Z)
empiricalModelParameters: T_min, T_max: daily minimum and maximum temperature ; m: hours after minimum temperature ; Y: day length ; a: lag of maximum temperature after noon ; T_sn: temperature at sunset ; b: nocturnal decay coefficient ; n: hours after sunset ; Z: night length

definition: A statistical analysis that quantifies the strength and direction of the linear association between two variables using the Pearson correlation coefficient.
comment: The coefficient is the covariance divided by the product of standard deviations, ranging from −1 to 1; it is used to assess relationships such as between solar irradiation and wind variables.

definition: A three-parameter continuous probability distribution equal to a gamma distribution with an added location parameter.
comment: It is used in hydrological frequency analysis of flows and has been fitted to wind speed data.
distributionFormula: f(x) = (x − a)^(s−1) exp[−(x − a)/b] / (b^s Γ(s)), for x ≥ a
distributionParameters: s: shape parameter ; b: scale parameter ; a: location parameter

definition: The Pearson type V distribution is a continuous distribution of the Pearson system equivalent to the inverse gamma distribution.
comment: It is fitted to wind-speed frequencies as an alternative to Weibull and gamma.
distributionParameters: α: shape parameter ; β: scale parameter

definition: A physically based combination equation that computes evapotranspiration from the surface energy balance and aerodynamic vapour transfer.
comment: It uses net radiation, temperature, humidity and wind speed; in its FAO-56 form it gives reference evapotranspiration used in hydrological and hydropower water balance studies.
physicalModelParameters: ET0: reference evapotranspiration (mm/day) ; Δ: slope of saturation vapour pressure curve ; R_n: net radiation ; G: soil heat flux ; γ: psychrometric constant ; T: mean air temperature (°C) ; u_2: wind speed at 2 m ; e_s: saturation vapour pressure ; e_a: actual vapour pressure
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: surface energy balance and aerodynamic mass transfer

definition: A continuous probability distribution defined by minimum, most likely and maximum values, constructed as a rescaled beta distribution.
comment: Its shape parameters are derived from the three estimates; it is used to represent uncertain inputs in risk and techno-economic analyses of energy projects.
distributionParameters: a: minimum ; m: most likely value ; b: maximum ; B: beta function

definition: Perturb and observe is a maximum power point tracking algorithm that iteratively perturbs the operating voltage of a PV system and observes the resulting change in power.
comment: If power increases the perturbation continues in the same direction, otherwise it is reversed, so the operating point oscillates around the maximum power point of PV modules.

definition: A thermodynamic model that gives the exergy content of thermal radiation as a function of the sun and ambient temperatures.
comment: The exergy-to-energy ratio is computed from the ratio of ambient to sun temperature and applied to direct and diffuse radiation, which are summed to obtain global solar exergy; it is used to assess the work potential of solar radiation.
physicalModelParameters: Ex: exergy of radiation ; E: radiation energy ; T0: ambient temperature (K) ; Ts: sun (radiation source) temperature (K)
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: second law of thermodynamics (exergy of radiation)

definition: A physical model that converts forecast irradiance into photovoltaic power output.
comment: It derives plane-of-array irradiance from NWP or irradiance forecasts and computes PV power through the photoelectric conversion of the modules, for PV power forecasting.
physicalModelParameters: I: current; V: voltage; I_sc: short-circuit current; V_oc: open-circuit voltage; V_mp,I_mp: maximum-power-point voltage/current; k_1,k_2: derived TRW model factors
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: TRW photovoltaic conversion model.

definition: Photovoltaic module energy-output equations are a physical model that computes PV module power or energy from incident irradiance and module temperature.
comment: Module efficiency is derated linearly with cell temperature and multiplied by irradiance and area; it is used to estimate PV energy yield from estimated radiation.
physicalModelFormula: P = η_ref A G [1 − β_ref (Tc − T_ref)]
physicalModelParameters: P: module power ; η_ref: reference efficiency ; A: module area ; G: plane-of-array irradiance ; β_ref: temperature coefficient of efficiency ; Tc: cell temperature ; T_ref: reference temperature
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: photovoltaic conversion of solar irradiance with temperature-dependent efficiency

definition: A physical model that computes photovoltaic power output from irradiance and module characteristics using constant parameters.
comment: Power is derived from physical relations of PV conversion efficiency and operating conditions; it is used as a baseline for PV power prediction.
physicalModelParameters: P_PV: photovoltaic power; GTI: global tilted irradiance; N_m: number of modules/subarrays; A_m: active module area; \eta_PV: module efficiency; \eta_inv: inverter efficiency; f_PV: derating factor; \gamma: temperature coefficient; T_c: cell temperature; T_{c,REF}: reference cell temperature
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Detailed photovoltaic model implemented in NREL System Advisor Model (SAM).

definition: An empirical wind-turbine power curve that approximates the manufacturer curve by linear interpolation between a few nodes.
comment: Power is zero below cut-in and above cut-out, linear between successive nodes and constant at rated power; it is used to convert wind speed to turbine power output.
empiricalModelFormula: P(v) = 0 for v < vci or v > vco ; P(v) = Pi + (Pi+1 − Pi)(v − vi)/(vi+1 − vi) for vi ≤ v < vi+1 ; P(v) = Pr for vr ≤ v ≤ vco
empiricalModelParameters: v: wind speed ; vci: cut-in speed ; vr: rated speed ; vco: cut-out speed ; vi, Pi: curve nodes ; Pr: rated power
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Pitch- or stall-regulated turbine with known power-curve nodes

definition: The Plackett bivariate distribution is a joint probability distribution built from the one-parameter Plackett copula linking two marginal distributions.
comment: The dependence parameter controls association between the variables, and it is used to model joint distributions such as wind speed and direction or wind speed and other meteorological variables.
distributionParameters: θ: Plackett dependence (odds-ratio) parameter ; F, G: marginal distribution functions

definition: A kernel density estimator whose bandwidth is selected by the plug-in method.
comment: The bandwidth is obtained by estimating the unknown functional of the density in the asymptotically optimal bandwidth formula; it is used to estimate wind-speed distributions without assuming a parametric form.
distributionFormula: f̂(v) = (1/(n h)) Σ(i=1 to n) K((v − v_i)/h)
distributionParameters: h: bandwidth (smoothing parameter) ; K: kernel function ; n: sample size ; v_i: observed values

definition: A spatially distributed hydrological model developed at Politecnico di Milano that simulates soil water balance and flow routing.
comment: It tracks daily cell-scale soil-water balance, snow and ice melt, and routes surface and subsurface flow, used to simulate streamflow for hydropower under climate change.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Distributed/cell-scale hydrological water-balance model with surface and subsurface flow routing.

definition: Poli-Power is a reservoir-operation optimization model that maximizes annual hydropower revenue under hydrological and operational constraints.
comment: It schedules releases and storage to maximize revenue subject to reservoir constraints; it is used for hydropower planning and operation studies.

definition: A regression model that estimates hydropower demand and normalized relative price from gross domestic product, temperature and random factors.
comment: It links economic and climatic drivers to hydropower demand and price.

definition: A regression model that expresses a dependent variable as a polynomial function of an independent variable.
comment: Coefficients are estimated by least squares; it is used when linear relations are insufficient, for example to describe the variation of the Weibull shape parameter with wind speed.

definition: The power-duration curve method is an empirical hydropower assessment method that converts a flow-duration curve into power available as a function of the percentage of time it is equalled or exceeded.
comment: Each exceedance discharge is converted to power with the hydropower equation, and the curve is used to derive firm power, design capacity and annual energy of run-of-river schemes.
empiricalModelFormula: P(p) = ρ g η H Q(p)
empiricalModelParameters: P(p): power equalled or exceeded p percent of the time ; Q(p): discharge from the flow-duration curve ; H: net head ; η: overall efficiency ; ρ: water density ; g: gravitational acceleration
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Mainly for run-of-river schemes with a representative flow record

definition: An empirical relation that extrapolates wind speed from a reference height to another height using a power function of the height ratio.
comment: The wind shear exponent depends on surface roughness and atmospheric stability; it is used to estimate wind speed at turbine hub height from measurements at lower heights.
empiricalModelParameters: v2: wind speed at height h2 ; v1: wind speed at reference height h1 ; h2: target height ; h1: reference height ; α: wind shear (power-law) exponent
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Near-neutral atmospheric stability over homogeneous terrain; α often taken as 1/7 for open terrain but site-specific

definition: A two-parameter continuous probability distribution obtained by a power transformation of the Lindley distribution.
comment: The additional shape parameter increases flexibility so that wind-speed datasets with different characteristics can be fitted.
distributionFormula: f(v) = [α β² / (β + 1)] (1 + v^α) v^(α−1) exp(−β v^α)
distributionParameters: α: shape parameter ; β: scale parameter

definition: Power regression is a regression model in which the response is a power function of the predictors, usually fitted by linear regression on log-transformed variables.
comment: It relates renewable power generation or resource variables to weather variables.

definition: An economic method that computes the present value of all costs of an energy project over its lifetime and the resulting cost of energy per kWh.
comment: Investment, discounted operation and maintenance costs and scrap value are combined using inflation and discount rates and divided by energy generated; it is used to assess wind-project economics.

definition: A photovoltaic performance model of the PVGIS tool that estimates PV power output from satellite-derived irradiance and temperature.
comment: It computes in-plane irradiance and applies an efficiency depending on irradiance and module temperature to rated power; it is used to estimate PV energy yield.
physicalModelFormula: P = Pnom (G/1000) ηrel(G′,T′) ; ηrel = 1 + k1 ln G′ + k2 (ln G′)² + T′(k3 + k4 ln G′ + k5 (ln G′)²) + k6 T′² ; G′ = G/1000 ; T′ = Tm − 25
physicalModelParameters: P: PV power output ; Pnom: nominal power at STC ; G: in-plane irradiance (W/m²) ; Tm: module temperature (°C) ; ηrel: relative efficiency ; k1-k6: technology-specific coefficients
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Photovoltaic conversion of irradiance with irradiance and temperature dependent efficiency

definition: Quadratic regression is a regression model that relates a response to a predictor through a second-degree polynomial.
comment: Coefficients are fitted by least squares, and it is used for instance to relate solar radiation to sunshine duration or other meteorological predictors.

definition: A structured planning method that translates requirements into prioritized technical responses through relationship matrices.
comment: Relationship matrices link needs or barriers to strategies and propagate importance weights to rank responses; it is used to map renewable-energy adoption barriers to mitigation strategies.

definition: A non-probability survey sampling technique that recruits respondents from target population groups until predefined quotas are met.
comment: It is used in surveys on renewable-energy adoption and perception; it is a data-collection method rather than a model.

definition: A study-specific empirical model that estimates the clearness index from the logarithm of the daily air-temperature range.
comment: Its coefficients were calibrated locally to estimate global solar radiation from temperature data.
empiricalModelParameters: R: clearness-index response used by the paper [-]; \Delta T=T_{\max}-T_{\min} [°C]; a,b: empirical coefficients

definition: A study-specific sunshine-based empirical model that estimates global solar radiation from relative sunshine duration.
comment: It is an Angstrom-type linear relation with locally fitted coefficients (0.22 and 0.43 in the source study) used to estimate global radiation where only sunshine data are available.
empiricalModelParameters: G_p: predicted monthly mean daily global solar radiation [MJ m^-2 day^-1]; G_o: monthly mean extraterrestrial solar radiation [MJ m^-2 day^-1]; n: monthly mean daily sunshine duration [h]; N: maximum monthly mean daily sunshine duration [h]; a,b: location-specific empirical coefficients [-]

definition: A study-specific empirical polynomial model that estimates daily global solar radiation from the diurnal temperature range.
comment: It was proposed and calibrated in a single study to predict solar radiation where only temperature data are available.
empiricalModelParameters: R_s: daily global solar radiation; R_a: extraterrestrial radiation; \Delta T=T_{\max}-T_{\min}; T: temperature term used in the paper; a,b,c,d,e: fitted coefficients

definition: Study-specific empirical models proposed to estimate solar radiation using temperature together with logarithmic precipitation and relative humidity terms.
comment: They extend temperature-based empirical correlations with precipitation and humidity predictors and are calibrated and compared with existing models in the source study.

definition: A study-specific group of empirical models that estimate diffuse solar radiation from the clearness index.
comment: The diffuse fraction is correlated with the clearness index using fitted regression forms; they are used to estimate diffuse radiation where only global radiation is measured.

definition: A study-specific set of empirical models that estimate diffuse solar radiation from several meteorological variables.
comment: The models combine sunshine duration, global radiation, temperature and relative humidity in regression equations for diffuse radiation estimation.

definition: A study-specific group of empirical models that estimate diffuse solar radiation from sunshine duration.
comment: They relate the diffuse fraction or diffuse clearness index to relative sunshine duration and are compared for diffuse-radiation estimation.

definition: A study-specific one-variable regression model that estimates global solar radiation from sunshine duration.
comment: It is one of several candidate sunshine-based models compared to estimate solar radiation at the study sites.

definition: A study-specific empirical regression model that estimates solar radiation from sunshine duration, latitude and altitude.
comment: It is calibrated on station data in a single study and used to estimate global solar radiation.

definition: A study-specific empirical regression model that estimates solar radiation from sunshine duration, latitude, altitude and relative humidity.
comment: It is one of several numbered models calibrated with station data and evaluated with statistical indicators in the source study.

definition: A study-specific set of 42 published temperature-based empirical models for estimating global solar radiation.
comment: The models relate solar radiation to air-temperature variables and were evaluated across six Moroccan climatic zones to identify the best-performing forms.

definition: A study-specific hybrid model in which a least-squares model is optimized with a decision-tree learner.
comment: It combines least-squares fitting with decision-tree learning to improve the prediction of the target renewable-energy variable.

definition: A study-specific linear-logarithmic empirical model that estimates solar radiation from relative sunshine duration.
comment: It combines linear and logarithmic sunshine terms with coefficients calibrated for Iranian stations.
empiricalModelParameters: H: global solar radiation; H_0: extraterrestrial radiation; n/N: relative sunshine duration; a,b,c: empirical coefficients
