definition: A study-specific nationally calibrated linear Angstrom–Prescott model that estimates global solar radiation from relative sunshine duration.
comment: It is one of several candidate models compared in the source study, with coefficients calibrated at national scale.
empiricalModelParameters: H: global solar radiation; H_0: extraterrestrial radiation; n/N: relative sunshine duration; a,b: Angstrom-Prescott coefficients

definition: A study-specific empirical model that estimates global solar radiation as a cubic function of relative sunshine duration.
comment: It is calibrated for Iranian stations and used to estimate solar radiation from sunshine measurements.
empiricalModelParameters: H: global solar radiation; H_0: extraterrestrial radiation; n/N: relative sunshine duration; a,b,c,d: empirical coefficients

definition: A study-specific empirical model that estimates solar radiation from average air temperature.
comment: It is one of several numbered models calibrated and compared in the source study.

definition: A study-specific exponential temperature-based empirical model for estimating solar radiation.
comment: It relates solar radiation to air temperature through an exponential function with locally fitted coefficients.

definition: A study-specific temperature-difference exponential empirical model for solar radiation estimation.
comment: It estimates solar radiation from the air temperature difference through an exponential relation, as one of several compared models.

definition: A study-specific linear empirical model that estimates solar radiation from the air-temperature difference.
comment: It relates the clearness index linearly to the daily temperature range and is compared with other empirical models.

definition: A study-specific empirical model that estimates global solar radiation from the logarithm of air temperature.
comment: It is one of several temperature-based candidate models compared to estimate solar radiation.

definition: A study-specific empirical model that estimates solar radiation from the logarithm of the air temperature difference.
comment: It is calibrated in a single study and used to estimate solar radiation where only temperature data are available.

definition: A study-specific linear regression model that estimates a target variable at a given site from meteorological predictors.
comment: Its coefficients are fitted by least squares to local data and it is compared with other models in the source study.

definition: A study-specific site-level regression model with logarithmic terms that estimates solar radiation from meteorological predictors.
comment: Coefficients are fitted to local meteorological data to estimate solar radiation at the study site.

definition: A study-specific quadratic regression model relating the target variable to meteorological predictors.
comment: Coefficients are fitted on site data to estimate the target variable, such as solar radiation, at the study location.

definition: A study-specific new empirical model proposed for solar-radiation estimation.
comment: It achieved the best reported statistical indicators (MPE, SSRE, RSE, RMSE, R²) among the compared models.

definition: A study-specific model, numbered 4 in the source study, recommended for its good accuracy.
comment: The source provides no further detail on its form; it was retained as the most accurate among the compared models.

definition: A study-specific set of twelve empirical correlations developed to estimate solar radiation.
comment: The correlations relate solar radiation to meteorological variables and are calibrated and compared within one study.

definition: A study-specific group of seven empirical models, six temperature-based and one based on temperature and precipitation, for estimating solar radiation.
comment: The models are calibrated with local meteorological data and compared with statistical indicators in the source study.

definition: A study-specific set of multiple linear regression models developed separately for each station.
comment: Each model relates the target renewable-energy variable to local meteorological predictors with station-specific coefficients.

definition: A study-specific group of empirical models that relate global solar radiation to sunshine duration.
comment: They are Angstrom-type regression equations fitted on site data and compared with other model groups.

definition: A study-specific group of empirical models that estimate solar radiation from maximum and minimum air temperature.
comment: They are temperature-based correlations compared for global solar-radiation estimation where sunshine data are lacking.

definition: A study-specific set of autoregressive and machine learning models evaluated at 5-minute, hourly and daily resolutions.
comment: It compares forecasting performance across temporal resolutions for renewable-energy time series.

definition: A study-specific set of three empirical models based on Angstrom-type relationships between solar radiation and sunshine duration.
comment: The models are calibrated on local data and compared to estimate global solar radiation.

definition: A study-specific group of six empirical models for estimating solar radiation from meteorological variables.
comment: They are calibrated and evaluated with statistical indicators in the source study to select the most suitable model.

definition: A feedforward neural network with a single hidden layer of radial basis function neurons and a linear output layer.
comment: Hidden neurons respond to the distance between inputs and their centres through Gaussian-type functions and outputs are linear combinations of these activations; it is used to predict solar radiation and wind speed.

definition: An ensemble learning method that aggregates many decision trees trained on bootstrap samples with random feature selection.
comment: Predictions are averaged (regression) or voted (classification) over trees, reducing variance; it is widely used to predict solar radiation, wind speed and power output.

definition: The Range of Variability Approach is a statistical method for assessing hydrologic alteration by comparing post-impact flow statistics with their natural range of variability.
comment: Indicators of hydrologic alteration are divided into categories based on the pre-impact distribution and alteration is computed from observed versus expected frequencies; it is used to evaluate the flow-regime impacts of dams and hydropower.

definition: A one-parameter continuous distribution that is a special case of the Weibull distribution with shape parameter 2.
comment: It describes the magnitude of a two-dimensional vector with independent Gaussian components; it is widely used to model wind-speed distributions when only the mean wind speed is known.
distributionFormula: f(v) = (v/σ²) exp[−v²/(2σ²)], v ≥ 0 (equivalently f(v) = (π v/(2 v̄²)) exp[−π v²/(4 v̄²)])
distributionParameters: σ: scale parameter (v̄: mean wind speed in the equivalent form)

definition: A four-parameter mixture distribution of a Rayleigh distribution for isotropic flow and a Rice distribution for persistent prevailing flow.
comment: The mixing weight balances random isotropic and channelled wind components; it is fitted to wind-speed frequency data.
distributionFormula: f(v) = α (v/σ1²) exp[−v²/(2σ1²)] + (1−α)(v/σ2²) exp[−(v² + μ²)/(2σ2²)] I0(v μ/σ2²)
distributionParameters: α: mixing weight ; σ1²: Rayleigh variance parameter ; μ: Rice noncentrality parameter (mean prevailing speed) ; σ2²: Rice variance parameter ; I0: modified Bessel function of the first kind of order zero

definition: The RCA4 three-member CORDEX-Africa ensemble is a regional climate model ensemble in which the Rossby Centre RCA4 model downscales three global climate models (HadGEM2-ES, IPSL-CM5A-MR, GFDL-ESM2M) over Africa.
comment: The members were selected for their skill in reproducing historical wind speed and the ensemble provides future wind-speed projections for wind-energy assessment.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Ensemble constructed from RCA4_HadGEM2-ES, RCA4_IPSL-CM5A-MR and RCA4_GFDL-ESM2M regional climate simulations.

definition: A neural network with recurrent connections that maintains a hidden state to process sequential data.
comment: The hidden state is updated at each time step from the current input and previous state, capturing temporal dependencies; it is used to forecast solar radiation, wind speed and power from meteorological time series.

definition: A review of policy instruments for renewable electricity against technological, economic and institutional barriers.
comment: It assesses how support instruments address barriers to renewable-electricity adoption; it is a policy analysis rather than a model.

definition: A residual neural network is a deep feedforward neural network that uses skip (identity) connections so that layers learn residual functions.
comment: Skip connections ease training of very deep networks by mitigating vanishing gradients; it is used for renewable-energy forecasting and estimation.

definition: A first-order training algorithm for neural networks that updates each weight using only the sign of its gradient with an adaptive step size.
comment: Step sizes grow while the gradient sign is stable and shrink when it changes; it is used to train ANNs predicting renewable-energy variables.

definition: A statistical modelling approach that fits low-order polynomial response surfaces to relate a response to several input factors.
comment: Second-order polynomial models are fitted to designed or observed data to explore and optimise responses; it is used to predict solar radiation and optimise energy processes.

definition: The Rician distribution is a two-parameter continuous probability distribution of the magnitude of a bivariate normal vector with non-zero mean.
comment: It generalizes the Rayleigh distribution and is fitted to wind-speed data as an alternative to the Weibull and Rayleigh distributions.
distributionParameters: ν: distance between the reference point and the centre of the bivariate distribution (non-centrality) ; σ: spread (scale) parameter ; I0: modified Bessel function of the first kind of order zero

definition: A linear regression model whose coefficients are estimated with an L2 penalty on their magnitude.
comment: The penalty shrinks coefficients to reduce variance and handle multicollinearity among predictors; it is used to predict solar radiation and energy output from correlated meteorological variables.

definition: A kernel density estimator whose bandwidth is chosen by the rule-of-thumb (Silverman) formula.
comment: The bandwidth is computed from the sample standard deviation and size assuming a normal reference, giving a quick non-parametric estimate of wind speed distributions.
distributionParameters: K: kernel function ; h: bandwidth ; σ̂: sample standard deviation ; n: sample size ; v_i: observations

definition: The Sabbagh model is an empirical model that estimates global solar radiation from sunshine duration, relative humidity, maximum temperature and latitude.
comment: It was developed for arid and semi-arid climates; it is used to estimate horizontal global solar radiation where pyranometer data are lacking.

definition: A conceptual rainfall–runoff model that represents soil moisture in upper and lower zone tension and free-water storages.
comment: It simulates runoff components and is often coupled with snow routines and routing schemes; it is used to simulate streamflow and reservoir inflow for hydropower.

definition: A swarm-intelligence metaheuristic inspired by the chain-swarming behaviour of salps.
comment: A leader salp moves toward the best food source while followers follow the chain; it is used to tune parameters of hybrid predictive models such as ANFIS.

definition: The SALSA framework is a systematic literature review methodology structured in Search, Appraisal, Synthesis and Analysis stages.
comment: It organizes evidence collection and evaluation in review studies, including reviews of renewable-energy research, and is a methodology rather than a model of a system.

definition: An empirical model that estimates photovoltaic module and cell temperature from irradiance, ambient temperature and wind speed.
comment: Module back-surface temperature increases with irradiance and decreases exponentially with wind speed, and cell temperature adds a conduction difference; it is used to correct PV performance predictions for temperature effects.
empiricalModelFormula: Tm = E exp(a + b WS) + Ta ; Tc = Tm + (E/E0) ΔT
empiricalModelParameters: Tm: module back-surface temperature (°C) ; Tc: cell temperature (°C) ; E: plane-of-array irradiance (W/m²) ; E0: reference irradiance (1000 W/m²) ; WS: wind speed (m/s) ; Ta: ambient temperature (°C) ; a: empirical coefficient for upper temperature limit ; b: empirical coefficient for wind-speed cooling ; ΔT: cell-to-module temperature difference at E0
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Coefficients depend on module type and mounting configuration

definition: A forecasting method that predicts surface solar irradiance hours ahead from geostationary satellite cloud information.
comment: Cloud fields derived from satellite images are extrapolated in time and converted to irradiance, for intraday solar power forecasting.
empiricalModelParameters: K_c: clear-sky index; n: cloud index; GHI: global horizontal irradiance; GHI_{cs}: clear-sky global horizontal irradiance
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Intraday horizons, daylight conditions

definition: Scaled conjugate gradient is a supervised training algorithm for neural networks that combines conjugate-gradient directions with a model-trust-region step scaling, avoiding line search.
comment: It minimizes network error efficiently with low memory use; it is used to train ANNs for solar and wind prediction.

definition: A four-electrode array configuration for vertical electrical sounding in which potential electrodes are closely spaced at the centre and current electrodes are progressively expanded.
comment: It is a geophysical survey layout used to measure apparent resistivity versus depth, for example in groundwater investigations.

definition: A time-series model that extends ARIMA with seasonal autoregressive, differencing and moving-average terms.
comment: It models series with periodic patterns after regular and seasonal differencing; it is used to forecast daily and monthly solar radiation and other seasonal energy series.
timeSeriesModelFormula: φp(B) ΦP(B^s) (1−B)^d (1−B^s)^D yt = θq(B) ΘQ(B^s) εt
timeSeriesModelParameters: SARIMA(p,d,q)(P,D,Q)s ; p: non-seasonal AR order ; d: non-seasonal differencing order ; q: non-seasonal MA order ; P: seasonal AR order ; D: seasonal differencing order ; Q: seasonal MA order ; s: season length ; B: backshift operator ; εt: white noise

modelName: seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average spatial insolation model
definition: The SARIMA spatial insolation model is a seasonal autoregressive integrated moving-average time-series model applied to forecast monthly insolation over a spatial region.
comment: It combines non-seasonal and seasonal autoregressive, differencing and moving-average terms to capture trend and annual cycle of insolation series at grid points or stations.
timeSeriesModelFormula: φ_p(B) Φ_P(B^s) (1 − B)^d (1 − B^s)^D y_t = θ_q(B) Θ_Q(B^s) ε_t
timeSeriesModelParameters: SARIMA(p,d,q)(P,D,Q)s ; p, q: non-seasonal AR and MA orders ; d: non-seasonal differencing order ; P, Q: seasonal AR and MA orders ; D: seasonal differencing order ; s: season length ; B: backshift operator ; ε_t: white noise

definition: An unsupervised neural network that maps high-dimensional inputs onto a low-dimensional grid of neurons while preserving topological relationships.
comment: Neurons compete for inputs and the winner and its neighbours are updated toward each input; it is used to cluster weather or resource patterns and partition input spaces for forecasting.

modelName: self-organizing map - support vector regression - particle swarm optimization hybrid model
definition: A hybrid model in which a self-organizing map partitions inputs, support vector regression models each region and particle swarm optimization tunes the SVR parameters.
comment: The clustering step creates locally specialised SVR models whose hyperparameters are selected by PSO, for forecasting variables such as wind or solar power.

definition: Semi-automatic narrow-valley selection is a GIS procedure that identifies narrow, highly suitable valleys as candidate dam or reservoir sites.
comment: It intersects contour lines with stream order and suitability within a stream buffer and queries narrow high-suitability valleys; it is used to screen hydropower or pumped-storage sites.

definition: An encoder–decoder model of long short-term memory networks that maps an input sequence to an output sequence.
comment: The encoder summarises past observations and the decoder generates multi-step predictions; it is used to forecast sequences of monthly renewable-energy variables.

modelName: Simple Membership Function and Fuzzy Rule Generating Technique
definition: A fuzzy-logic modelling technique that builds a model from simple membership functions and expert-generated fuzzy rules.
comment: Membership functions and rules are defined from the data range and physical reasoning rather than by training; it is used to estimate solar radiation.

definition: Simulated annealing is a probabilistic metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the annealing of metals that accepts worse solutions with a probability decreasing with a temperature parameter.
comment: The gradual cooling schedule lets the search escape local optima; it is used to calibrate models such as ANNs and to optimize renewable-energy system design.

definition: A study-specific set of six empirical functions that approximate the wind-turbine output power curve.
comment: Each function relates turbine power output to wind speed between cut-in, rated and cut-out speeds; they are compared to estimate turbine energy production.

definition: A flexible continuous probability distribution family that extends the generalized error distribution with skewness.
comment: Its shape parameters control kurtosis and skewness, allowing asymmetric wind-speed distributions to be modelled.
distributionFormula: f(x; μ, σ, λ, p) = p · exp( −( |x − μ + m| / ( vσ(1 + λ·sign(x − μ + m)) ) )^p ) / ( 2vσΓ(1/p) ) ; m = 2^(2/p)·vσλ·Γ(1/2 + 1/p)/√π ; v = [ π(1 + 3λ²)Γ(3/p) − 16^(1/p)·λ²·Γ(1/2 + 1/p)² / (Γ(1/p)√π) ]^(−1/2) (v = 1, m = 0 without variance/mean adjustment)
distributionParameters: μ: location ; σ: scale (σ > 0) ; λ: skewness (−1 < λ < 1) ; p: shape controlling peakedness/kurtosis (p > 0)

definition: The skewed t distribution is a flexible continuous distribution family that generalizes the Student t distribution with a skewness parameter.
comment: One shape parameter controls tail heaviness and another adjusts skewness; it is used to model wind-speed distributions.
distributionParameters: η: degrees of freedom (2 < η < ∞) ; λ: skewness (−1 < λ < 1)

modelName: slime mould optimized support vector regression
definition: A hybrid model in which the hyperparameters of support vector regression are tuned by the Slime Mould Algorithm.
comment: The metaheuristic searches SVR parameters to minimise prediction error; it is used to predict renewable-energy variables.

definition: A hybrid model in which the hyperparameters of an XGBoost gradient-boosting model are tuned by the slime mould algorithm.
comment: The metaheuristic searches the boosting hyperparameters to minimise prediction error; it is used to forecast renewable-energy variables.

modelName: small hydropower resource assessment and sustainability analysis model
definition: The small hydropower resource assessment and sustainability analysis model is a decision-support framework that identifies and screens candidate small hydropower sites by resource potential, energy cost and emissions.
comment: Candidate sites are evaluated with project-identification parameters to estimate potential, cost of energy and emission benefits, supporting sustainable small hydropower planning.

definition: A reference forecasting model that assumes the clear-sky index persists from the current time to the forecast horizon.
comment: The current ratio of measured to clear-sky irradiance is multiplied by the clear-sky irradiance at the target time; it is used as a baseline to evaluate solar irradiance forecasting models.
timeSeriesModelParameters: Î(t + Δt): forecast irradiance ; I(t): measured irradiance at time t ; Ics: clear-sky irradiance ; Δt: forecast horizon

definition: A semi-distributed, physically based watershed model that simulates hydrology, sediment and water quality at the basin scale.
comment: The watershed is divided into subbasins and hydrologic response units where the water balance is computed daily; it is used to simulate streamflow for hydropower potential and climate impact studies.
physicalModelParameters: SW_t: final soil-water content; SW_0: initial soil-water content; R_day: precipitation; Q_sur: surface runoff; E_a: evapotranspiration; W_seep: percolation/bypass from soil profile; Q_gw: return flow/groundwater contribution
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: SWAT hydrologic cycle based on the watershed water-balance equation.

definition: SolarGIS is a satellite-based solar-resource model and database that derives solar irradiance from satellite imagery and atmospheric data.
comment: It combines clear-sky radiative modelling with cloud information from geostationary satellites; its estimates serve as reference data in solar-resource assessment and model validation.

definition: A commercial solar resource database and photovoltaic energy-yield simulation tool.
comment: It provides satellite-derived irradiation data such as monthly average daily GHI and estimates PV system energy output for site assessment.

definition: An empirical model, adapted from the SOYGRO crop model, that estimates photovoltaic module temperature from meteorological conditions.
comment: It relates module temperature to ambient conditions such as air temperature and irradiance; it is used to correct PV output for temperature effects.
empiricalModelParameters: T(t): hourly temperature; T_min(n),T_max(n): daily minimum/maximum temperature; \tau: time-angle term defined by the paper

definition: Spikeslab is a Bayesian variable-selection regression method that uses spike-and-slab priors on coefficients combined with model averaging.
comment: The spike concentrates negligible coefficients near zero and the slab allows large ones, so relevant predictors are selected while predictions are averaged over models for forecasting renewable-energy variables.

definition: An ensemble square-root data-assimilation filter that updates the ensemble mean and anomalies deterministically without perturbing observations.
comment: Model forecasts are combined with observations to update state variables in a square-root form of the Kalman analysis; it is used to update hydrological model water components with satellite observations.

definition: A qualitative analysis of technical, financial, policy, social and cultural barriers to renewable energy from the perspective of stakeholder groups.
comment: It synthesizes barriers as seen by government, private sector, financial institutions, communities and international organizations; it is an analysis rather than a model.

definition: A study-specific empirical power curve of a standard 2.5 MW wind turbine giving power output as a function of hub-height wind speed.
comment: Discrete manufacturer power-curve values are interpolated with a spline to obtain a continuous curve used to estimate turbine energy production.

definition: A maximum power point tracking controller that sets the PV operating voltage from extended Kalman filter estimates of temperature and irradiance.
comment: The estimated states determine the voltage corresponding to the maximum power point; it is used to maximise PV energy extraction.

definition: A method that derives local-scale climate variables from coarse climate-model output using statistical relationships with observations.
comment: Statistical transfer functions or bias corrections link large-scale model output to station data; it is used to project local temperature, precipitation and renewable resources under climate change.

definition: The Strahler stream-order method is a hierarchical classification scheme that assigns orders to stream segments in a drainage network according to their tributary structure.
comment: First-order streams have no tributaries and the order increases by one only where two streams of equal order join; it is used in GIS analyses of river networks for hydropower site identification.

definition: The Sequential Uncertainty Fitting version 2 procedure for calibrating hydrological model parameters and quantifying their uncertainty.
comment: Parameter ranges are iteratively narrowed by Latin hypercube sampling to bracket observations within a 95 percent prediction uncertainty band; it is used in SWAT-CUP to calibrate SWAT streamflow simulations for hydropower studies.

definition: A kernel-based supervised learning model that finds a maximum-margin hyperplane in a feature space.
comment: Through kernel functions and an epsilon-insensitive loss (support vector regression) it captures nonlinear relationships; it is used to estimate solar radiation and forecast wind speed and power.

modelName: support vector machine time-series forecasting model
definition: An SVM time-series forecasting model is a support vector regression model that predicts future values from lagged observations.
comment: Lagged irradiance values are mapped through a kernel to a regression function with an epsilon-insensitive loss; it is used for short-term solar irradiance forecasting.

definition: A kernel-based regression model that fits a function within an ε-insensitive margin while minimising model complexity.
comment: It maps inputs to a high-dimensional feature space via kernels and solves a convex optimisation; it is used to predict solar radiation and wind speed and to approximate wind-speed distributions.

modelName: support vector regression - Boruta feature selection - grasshopper optimization algorithm hybrid model
definition: A hybrid model combining support vector regression with Boruta feature selection and grasshopper optimisation of hyperparameters.
comment: Boruta selects relevant predictors and the grasshopper algorithm tunes the SVR parameters; it is used to predict solar radiation or other renewable-energy variables.

definition: SVM-Firefly is a hybrid model in which the hyperparameters of a support vector machine are optimized by the firefly algorithm.
comment: The firefly metaheuristic, based on light-intensity attraction between fireflies, searches the SVM penalty and kernel parameters; it is used to predict monthly global solar radiation.

definition: A hybrid model in which support vector regression parameters are optimized by the Krill Herd metaheuristic.
comment: The Krill Herd algorithm searches the SVR hyperparameter space to minimise prediction error, here using data from neighbouring stations; it is used to estimate solar radiation.

definition: A hydrological data assimilation system that couples the SWAT model with the PDAF data assimilation framework.
comment: Model and observation files are read offline, states are updated by assimilation and the updated states are used to continue the SWAT simulation, improving streamflow simulation.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Offline hydrological data-assimilation system coupling SWATGP with the Parallel Data Assimilation Framework (PDAF), reading model/observation states, assimilating them, and writing updated states.

definition: A hybrid modelling system that combines Kappa, Wakeby and Burr–generalized extreme value mixture wind-speed distributions with a random forests classifier that selects among them.
comment: The classifier chooses the most suitable distribution for each wind-speed dataset; it is used for wind-speed distribution modelling.

definition: A conceptual theory explaining technology adoption through perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use.
comment: These perceptions shape attitudes and intentions to use a technology; it is used to analyse adoption of renewable-energy technologies.

definition: The technology-maturity framework is a conceptual framework that classifies energy technologies by stage of development from basic and applied research to commercial deployment.
comment: Technologies are placed in stages such as R&D, demonstration, pre-commercial, supported commercial and commercial, which guides assessment of renewable-energy technologies and policy support.

definition: A study-specific hourly wind-energy calculation that adjusts turbine output for air temperature and air density.
comment: Hourly electrical energy is computed from rotor diameter, air density, temperature, wind speed, a logical temperature function and a turbine-efficiency polynomial; it is used to estimate energy yield under local atmospheric conditions.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: kinetic energy flux of the wind

modelName: temperature-radiation empirical relation - fitted regression hybrid model 5
definition: A study-specific combined empirical model that couples a temperature-based radiation relation with fitted regression coefficients to estimate global solar radiation.
comment: It is one of six combined models in the study that estimate global solar radiation from temperature data.
empiricalModelParameters: x: measured daily global solar radiation term used in fitted regression; G_0: daily extraterrestrial radiation [Wh m^-2 day^-1]; \Delta T: daily temperature range [°C]; a_1,b_1,a,b,c: fitted empirical coefficients; f(T): temperature function as defined in the paper

definition: The theoretical hydropower line-potential equation is a physical model that computes the gross hydropower potential of a river reach from mean discharge and elevation drop.
comment: Line potential is the product of water density, gravity, mean annual discharge and head drop of the reach, and specific potential divides it by reach length; it is used for basin-scale hydropower potential mapping.
physicalModelFormula: P_line = ρ g Q ΔH ; P_spec = P_line / L
physicalModelParameters: P_line: theoretical line potential ; ρ: water density ; g: gravitational acceleration ; Q: mean annual discharge ; ΔH: elevation drop of the reach ; L: reach length ; P_spec: specific potential per unit length
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: gravitational potential energy of flowing water

definition: A physical equation that gives the theoretical power of wind passing through a rotor swept area.
comment: Power equals half the air density times the swept area times the cube of wind speed; it is used to estimate available wind power.
physicalModelParameters: P: theoretical wind power ; ρ: air density ; A: rotor swept area ; v: wind speed
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: kinetic energy flux

definition: A conceptual theory of behaviour in which attitudes, subjective norms and perceived behavioural control determine intentions and actions.
comment: It is used to explain and predict individual intentions to adopt renewable energy or energy-saving behaviour.

definition: The thermal-storage wind-CSP system model is a hybrid energy-system model coupling wind farm, concentrated solar power, thermal energy storage and electric-heater submodels.
comment: The submodels are linked through steady-state energy-flow constraints so that surplus wind electricity heats the thermal storage, enabling assessment of dispatchability and performance of combined wind-CSP plants.

definition: An empirical temperature-based equation for estimating monthly potential evapotranspiration.
comment: It relates potential evapotranspiration to mean monthly air temperature through an annual heat index, corrected for day length; it is used in water-balance and hydrological studies when only temperature data are available.
empiricalModelParameters: PET: monthly potential evapotranspiration (mm/month) ; L: average day length (hours) ; N: number of days in the month ; Ta: mean monthly air temperature (°C) ; I: annual heat index ; Ti: mean temperature of month i (°C) ; a: empirical exponent
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Monthly time step; mean air temperature above 0 °C; tends to underestimate in arid climates

definition: A finite mixture distribution formed by a weighted sum of three two-parameter Weibull distributions.
comment: Each Weibull component has its own shape and scale, allowing multimodal wind-speed regimes to be represented.
distributionFormula: f(v) = Σ_(i=1..3) w_i (k_i/c_i)(v/c_i)^(k_i−1) exp[−(v/c_i)^(k_i)], with Σ w_i = 1
distributionParameters: w_i: weight of component i ; k_i: shape parameter of component i ; c_i: scale parameter of component i

definition: The three-parameter lognormal distribution is a shifted lognormal distribution whose logarithm of the variable minus a location (threshold) parameter is normally distributed.
comment: The location parameter sets a lower bound; it is used to fit wind-speed and hydrological frequency distributions.
distributionParameters: γ: location (threshold) parameter ; μ: mean of ln(x − γ) ; σ: standard deviation of ln(x − γ)

definition: An ideal single-diode equivalent-circuit model of a photovoltaic cell defined by three parameters without series or shunt resistance.
comment: The current–voltage characteristic is computed from the photocurrent, diode saturation current and ideality factor; it is used to predict PV cell and module power.
physicalModelParameters: I_ph: photocurrent ; I_0: diode saturation current ; n: diode ideality factor ; V_t: thermal voltage kT/q
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: photovoltaic effect and Kirchhoff current law applied to the Shockley diode equation

definition: A Weibull distribution with shape, scale and location parameters, the location setting a lower bound of the variable.
comment: The location parameter shifts the distribution so that it starts at a threshold; it is fitted to wind-speed data as an extension of the two-parameter Weibull law.
distributionParameters: k: shape parameter ; c: scale parameter ; γ: location parameter

definition: A time-delay neural network is a feedforward neural network whose inputs include time-delayed copies of the signal so that it learns temporal patterns.
comment: A tapped delay line feeds past values to the hidden layers, and it is used for time-series prediction of renewable-energy variables, for example one network per identified pattern cluster.

definition: A two-parameter continuous probability distribution obtained by applying the Topp-Leone generator to the Lindley distribution.
comment: The Topp-Leone shape parameter adds flexibility to the Lindley baseline, allowing it to fit skewed positive data; it is used to model wind-speed distributions.
distributionParameters: a: Topp-Leone shape parameter ; λ: Lindley parameter

definition: A conceptual framework that explains socio-technical transitions through interactions between niches, regimes and the landscape.
comment: It is used to analyse energy transitions and the diffusion of renewable-energy technologies.

definition: The trapezoidal rule is a numerical integration method that approximates the area under a curve by summing trapezoids between sampled points.
comment: In hydropower studies it is used to compute the area under flow- or power-duration curves to estimate energy.

definition: A two-component mixture of normal distributions truncated below zero to exclude negative wind speeds.
comment: It captures bimodal wind regimes with a weighted sum of two normals renormalised over positive values; it is fitted to wind-speed data for wind resource assessment.
distributionParameters: ω: mixing weight ; μ1, μ2: component means ; σ1, σ2: component standard deviations ; Φ: standard normal cumulative distribution function

definition: A mixture distribution formed by a weighted sum of two inverse Gaussian distributions.
comment: The mixing weight combines two inverse Gaussian components to capture bimodal wind regimes; it is fitted to wind-speed frequency data.
distributionFormula: f(v) = Σ_{i=1}^{2} ωi √(λi/(2π v³)) exp[−λi (v − μi)²/(2 μi² v)], ω1 + ω2 = 1
distributionParameters: ωi: mixing weights ; μi: component means ; λi: component shape parameters

definition: The two-way interaction ensemble is a hybrid divide-and-conquer ensemble that uses two-way feature interactions, LASSO input selection and glowworm-optimized combination weights.
comment: Submodels built on pairwise feature interactions are selected with LASSO and combined with weights tuned by glowworm swarm optimization to predict renewable-energy variables.

definition: A continuous probability distribution in which all values within a bounded interval are equally likely.
comment: Its density is constant between lower and upper bounds; it is used to represent bounded uncertain inputs such as normalized air density in probabilistic wind-energy analyses.
distributionFormula: f(x) = 1 / (b − a) for a ≤ x ≤ b, 0 otherwise
distributionParameters: a: lower bound ; b: upper bound

modelName: United Nations Industrial Development Organization gross hydropower potential model
definition: A physical equation that computes gross hydropower potential from discharge, gross head and overall efficiency.
comment: It applies the hydropower power equation to discharge and head data to estimate the hydropower potential of sites or basins.
physicalModelFormula: P = η ρ g Q H
physicalModelParameters: P: power ; η: overall efficiency ; ρ: water density ; g: gravitational acceleration ; Q: water discharge ; H: gross head
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Conservation of energy (potential energy of water)

modelName: Upper Benue small hydropower dam suitability model
definition: A study-specific GIS multi-criteria suitability model that classifies the Upper Benue basin into small-hydropower dam-site suitability classes.
comment: Ten thematic layers are reclassified, weighted and overlaid to produce five suitability classes for siting small hydropower dams.

definition: A Weibull distribution truncated above a maximum value, which contains the usual Weibull distribution as a limiting case.
comment: Truncation at an upper wind speed bounds the support; it is fitted to wind-speed data for wind resource assessment.
distributionParameters: k: scale parameter ; p: shape parameter ; T: truncation point

definition: An empirical wind-profile power law whose exponent varies with the reference wind speed and height.
comment: The exponent is computed from the reference wind speed instead of being fixed, then used to extrapolate wind speed to another height; it is used to estimate hub-height wind resources.
empiricalModelParameters: v1: wind speed at reference height ; v2: wind speed at target height ; h1: reference height (m) ; h2: target height (m) ; α: variable power-law exponent
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Neutral stability, flat terrain, reference height near 10 m

definition: The Variable Infiltration Capacity model is a semi-distributed macroscale hydrological model that solves the land-surface water and energy balances on a grid.
comment: It represents subgrid variability in soil infiltration capacity and vegetation to simulate runoff and baseflow, and is used with routing to estimate discharge for hydropower assessment.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Variable Infiltration Capacity land-surface hydrological model representing water and energy balance and runoff generation from meteorological forcing.

definition: A channel flow routing method that computes outflow from a reach using a storage coefficient based on travel time.
comment: Reach outflow is derived from the continuity equation with storage proportional to outflow and travel time; it is used in SWAT to route water through the channel network in hydrological and hydropower studies.

definition: A stream-gauging method that computes discharge as the product of cross-sectional area and mean flow velocity.
comment: The cross-section is divided into verticals where velocity is measured and partial discharges are summed; it is used to measure river discharge for hydropower assessment.
physicalModelParameters: Q: discharge ; v_i: mean velocity in subsection i ; A_i: area of subsection i
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Continuity (conservation of mass)

definition: The Vergnet GEV HP is a 1 MW two-bladed tiltable wind turbine designed for remote and cyclone-prone sites.
comment: It was selected for the Ashegoda wind farm and suits remote sites with limited access and lifting infrastructure.

definition: A geophysical survey technique that measures apparent ground resistivity at increasing electrode spacings to infer subsurface layering.
comment: It is used to characterise aquifers and validate groundwater potential maps.

definition: A rule-based expert system implemented in Visual Basic that supports the identification and ranking of hydropower sites.
comment: Rules extract and present satellite-derived terrain and hydrological features to evaluate candidate sites; it is used in hydropower site selection.

definition: The von Mises mixture distribution is a finite weighted mixture of von Mises circular distributions.
comment: Each component describes a preferred direction with its concentration, so the mixture represents multimodal wind-direction distributions in wind-resource assessment.
distributionFormula: f(θ) = Σ(j=1 to N) ω_j exp[κ_j cos(θ − μ_j)] / [2π I0(κ_j)], Σ ω_j = 1
distributionParameters: ω_j: weight of component j ; κ_j: concentration parameter of component j ; μ_j: mean direction of component j ; N: number of components ; I0: modified Bessel function of the first kind of order zero

definition: A five-parameter continuous probability distribution defined through its quantile function that generalizes several common distributions.
comment: Its flexible quantile form can mimic lognormal, Pearson type III and other shapes and is usually fitted by L-moments; it is used to model wind-speed and flood distributions.
distributionFormula: Quantile function: x(F) = ξ + (α/β)[1 − (1 − F)^β] − (γ/δ)[1 − (1 − F)^(−δ)]
distributionParameters: ξ: location parameter ; α: first scale parameter ; β: first shape parameter ; γ: second scale parameter ; δ: second shape parameter

definition: A model-evaluation procedure that repeatedly fits on past data and tests on the next period, preserving temporal order.
comment: It is used to evaluate time-series forecasting models of wind, solar or load; it is a validation procedure rather than a model.

definition: The Wang–Sheeley–Arge model is a semi-empirical coronal model that derives solar-wind speed and magnetic field at the inner heliosphere from photospheric magnetograms.
comment: It uses potential-field source-surface and Schatten current-sheet extrapolations with an empirical speed relation, providing boundary conditions for the ENLIL heliospheric model in space-weather forecasting.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Coronal model used to provide solar-wind inner-boundary conditions to ENLIL.

definition: A mathematical model that estimates photovoltaic module operating temperature from environmental conditions.
comment: Module temperature estimates are used to correct PV efficiency and power output.
empiricalModelParameters: T(t): hourly temperature; T_ave=(T_max+T_min)/2; T_amp=(T_max-T_min)/2; t_sr: sunrise time; t_max: time of maximum temperature; t_srn: sunset time

modelName: Weather Research and Forecasting hydrological modeling system
definition: A community hydrological modelling system that couples the Noah-MP land-surface model with high-resolution terrain and channel routing.
comment: It can run standalone or coupled to the WRF atmospheric model to simulate streamflow, soil moisture and runoff; it is used for flood forecasting and water-resource studies relevant to hydropower.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: WRF-Hydro couples land-surface hydrology with surface/subsurface/channel routing; the paper describes diffusive-wave surface routing and channel-routing components.

definition: The Weather Research and Forecasting model is a mesoscale numerical weather prediction and atmospheric simulation system.
comment: It solves the compressible non-hydrostatic equations with physics parameterizations on nested grids and is used to forecast or downscale wind and solar resources.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Weather Research and Forecasting mesoscale numerical weather prediction model used to generate the baseline solar-radiation forecast.

modelName: Weather Research and Forecasting Solar model
definition: A configuration of the Weather Research and Forecasting numerical weather prediction model augmented for solar-energy applications.
comment: It adds improved radiation, aerosol and cloud parameterizations and outputs direct and diffuse irradiance; it is used for operational solar irradiance and PV power forecasting.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: WRF-ARW Solar mesoscale numerical weather prediction chain for solar irradiance forecasting.

definition: An equation that computes mean wind power density from the parameters of the Weibull distribution of wind speed.
comment: The kinetic energy flux is integrated over the Weibull wind-speed distribution, giving power density from air density, scale and shape; it is used in wind resource assessment.
physicalModelParameters: ρ: air density ; c: Weibull scale parameter ; k: Weibull shape parameter
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Kinetic energy flux of the wind

definition: The Weibull distribution is a two-parameter continuous probability distribution for positive variables defined by a shape and a scale parameter.
comment: It is the standard model of wind-speed frequency distributions in wind resource assessment, used to derive mean power density and energy yield.
distributionParameters: k: shape parameter ; c: scale parameter

definition: A two-component heterogeneous mixture distribution formed by the weighted sum of a Weibull distribution and a generalized extreme value distribution.
comment: The components capture different wind regimes and tail behaviour; it is considered for wind-speed modelling in resource assessment.
distributionParameters: ω: mixing weight ; ξ: GEV shape parameter ; σ: GEV scale parameter ; μ: GEV location parameter ; k: Weibull shape parameter ; c: Weibull scale parameter

definition: A two-component heterogeneous mixture distribution combining a Weibull distribution and a Gumbel (extreme value type I) distribution.
comment: A mixing weight blends the two component densities to represent heterogeneous wind regimes; it is fitted to wind-speed frequency data.
distributionParameters: ω: mixing weight ; k: Weibull shape parameter ; c: Weibull scale parameter ; μ: Gumbel location parameter ; σ: Gumbel scale parameter

definition: The Weibull-inverse Gaussian mixture distribution is a two-component finite mixture probability distribution that combines a Weibull distribution and an inverse Gaussian distribution.
comment: The weighted combination captures bimodal or skewed wind-speed regimes and is compared with single and other mixture laws for wind-speed distribution fitting.
distributionParameters: ω: mixing weight ; k: Weibull shape parameter ; c: Weibull scale parameter ; μ: inverse Gaussian mean parameter ; λ: inverse Gaussian shape parameter

definition: A two-component heterogeneous mixture distribution composed of a Weibull and a Normal probability density.
comment: A mixing weight combines the two components to capture bimodal wind regimes; it is used to fit wind-speed frequency distributions.
distributionParameters: w: mixing weight ; k: Weibull shape parameter ; c: Weibull scale parameter ; μ: Normal mean ; σ: Normal standard deviation

definition: An empirical formula that assigns exceedance probabilities to ranked observations.
comment: Ranked flows are converted to the percentage of time each discharge is equalled or exceeded, building flow duration curves for hydropower assessment.
empiricalModelParameters: P: exceedance probability (%) ; m: rank of the observation in descending order ; n: number of observations
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Flow duration curve construction from ranked records

definition: The Weibull–Weibull mixture distribution is a two-component mixture of Weibull probability densities with a mixing weight.
comment: It models bimodal wind-speed regimes better than a single Weibull distribution in wind resource assessment.
distributionParameters: w: mixing weight (0 ≤ w ≤ 1) ; k1, k2: shape parameters ; c1, c2: scale parameters

definition: A two-parameter weighted version of the Lindley distribution.
comment: It offers flexible density and hazard shapes for positive data; it is fitted to wind-speed data as an alternative to the Weibull distribution.
distributionParameters: θ: scale-type parameter ; c: shape parameter

modelName: weighted-sum geographic information system multi-criteria evaluation
definition: A GIS-based multi-criteria evaluation method that combines reclassified criterion maps by a weighted sum.
comment: Criterion layers are standardised, weighted and overlaid to produce a suitability map; it is used for siting wind, solar and hydropower plants.

definition: A wide neural network is a feedforward neural network with a single fully connected hidden layer containing a large number of neurons (typically 100) with ReLU activation.
comment: It is a preset network architecture compared with other learners for predicting continuous renewable-energy variables.

definition: A study-specific empirical method for estimating Weibull parameters from the proportionality between the scale parameter and mean wind speed.
comment: It uses the relative difference between average wind power and the power at average wind speed to determine the Weibull parameters; it is used in wind resource assessment.

definition: A set of equations that compute available wind power density and the maximum recoverable power using the Betz limit.
comment: Available power density is the kinetic energy flux of the wind, and recoverable power is the Betz fraction 16/27 of it, used in wind resource assessment.
physicalModelParameters: ρ ; v
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Kinetic energy flux; Betz limit

definition: The wind power density equation is a physical model giving the power of the wind per unit swept area as a function of air density and wind speed.
comment: Mean power density is computed from the cube of wind speeds weighted by their frequencies (or a fitted distribution); it is used to classify wind resources at candidate sites.
physicalModelFormula: P/A = ½ ρ v³ ; mean: PD = ½ ρ Σ v_i³ f(v_i)
physicalModelParameters: P/A, PD: wind power density ; ρ: air density ; v, v_i: wind speed ; f(v_i): frequency of wind speed v_i
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: kinetic energy flux of moving air

definition: A physical equation that expresses the power of an airstream through a given area as proportional to the cube of wind speed.
comment: Power equals half the air density times the area times the cube of wind speed; it is used to compute wind power and wind power density.
physicalModelParameters: P: wind power ; ρ: air density ; A: area perpendicular to the flow ; v: wind speed
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: kinetic energy flux

definition: A physical model that estimates the power extracted by a wind turbine from the kinetic energy flux of the wind.
comment: Available wind power through the rotor area is scaled by the power coefficient; it is used to estimate wind-turbine output and wind energy potential.
physicalModelFormula: P = ½ ρ A v³ Cp
physicalModelParameters: P: power ; ρ: air density ; A: rotor swept area ; v: wind speed ; Cp: power coefficient
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: kinetic energy flux

modelName: wind profile log law and wind power density calculation
definition: The wind profile log law and wind power density calculation is a combined procedure that extrapolates wind speed vertically with the logarithmic profile and computes wind power density from the resulting wind-speed distribution.
comment: Measured 10 m wind speeds are extrapolated to hub height using surface roughness, and power density is obtained from air density and the Weibull distribution parameters at that height.
physicalModelParameters: v(z): wind speed at height z ; z_r: reference height ; z0: surface roughness length ; P/A: wind power density ; ρ: air density ; c: Weibull scale parameter ; k: Weibull shape parameter
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Kinetic energy flux with neutral surface-layer similarity

definition: A set of empirical relations that extrapolate wind speed and Weibull parameters from a reference height to another height.
comment: Wind speed and the Weibull scale parameter follow a power law with height while the shape parameter follows a logarithmic correction; it is used to estimate hub-height wind resources.
empiricalModelParameters: v ; v0 ; z ; z0 ; α ; kz ; k0 ; cz ; c0

definition: An empirical power-law relation that extrapolates wind speed from a measurement height to a reference height.
comment: Wind speed at the target height is the measured speed multiplied by the height ratio raised to the shear exponent; it is used when only 10 m data are available.
empiricalModelParameters: α
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Neutral stability, homogeneous terrain; measurement height typically 10 m

definition: Wind-speed vertical extrapolation by the power law is an empirical model that estimates wind speed at a target height from a reference height using a wind-shear exponent.
comment: Wind speed scales with the ratio of heights raised to the shear exponent; it is used to estimate hub-height wind speed from 10 m measurements.
empiricalModelParameters: v2: wind speed at height h2 ; v1: wind speed at reference height h1 ; α: wind-shear (power-law) exponent
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: α depends on surface roughness and atmospheric stability

modelName: wind turbine annual energy output equation
definition: A physical equation that estimates the annual energy output of a wind turbine from wind power, power coefficient and hours per year.
comment: The extractable power ½ρAV³Cp is multiplied by 8760 hours; it is used to estimate annual turbine energy yield.
physicalModelFormula: E = ½ ρ A V³ C_p × 8760
physicalModelParameters: E: annual energy output ; ρ: air density ; A: rotor swept area ; V: wind speed ; C_p: power coefficient ; 8760: hours per year
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: kinetic energy flux and energy as time integral of power

modelName: wind turbine electrical power output and capacity-factor calculation
definition: An empirical model that computes wind-turbine electrical power output from a parametric power curve and derives average power and capacity factor from Weibull wind statistics.
comment: The power curve is integrated over the Weibull wind-speed distribution to give mean power, divided by rated power to give capacity factor; it is used to compare turbines at candidate sites.
empiricalModelFormula: Pe(v) = Pr (v^k − vc^k)/(vr^k − vc^k) for vc ≤ v < vr ; Pe(v) = Pr for vr ≤ v ≤ vf ; Pe(v) = 0 otherwise ; Pe,ave = Pr {[exp(−(vc/c)^k) − exp(−(vr/c)^k)] / [(vr/c)^k − (vc/c)^k] − exp(−(vf/c)^k)} ; CF = Pe,ave/Pr
empiricalModelParameters: Pe: electrical power output ; Pr: rated power ; vc: cut-in speed ; vr: rated speed ; vf: cut-out speed ; k: Weibull shape parameter ; c: Weibull scale parameter ; Pe,ave: average power output ; CF: capacity factor
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Weibull-distributed hub-height wind speeds

modelName: wind turbine electrical power output simulation
definition: The wind turbine electrical power output simulation is a piecewise empirical power-curve model that gives turbine electrical output as a function of wind speed between cut-in, rated and cut-off speeds.
comment: Output is zero below cut-in and above cut-off speed, rises between cut-in and rated speed and equals rated power up to cut-off; it is used to estimate energy yield and capacity factor from wind data.
empiricalModelFormula: P(v) = 0 for v < v_ci or v > v_co ; P(v) = P_r (v^n − v_ci^n)/(v_r^n − v_ci^n) for v_ci ≤ v < v_r ; P(v) = P_r for v_r ≤ v ≤ v_co
empiricalModelParameters: P_r: rated electrical power ; v_ci: cut-in wind speed ; v_r: rated wind speed ; v_co: cut-off wind speed ; n: exponent of the rising segment (commonly 1, 2 or 3)
empiricalModelApplicabilityConditions: Steady wind at hub height; idealized turbine power curve

definition: An empirical model that estimates wind-turbine electrical output as a function of wind speed.
comment: Output is represented between cut-in, rated and cut-out wind speeds, typically by a fitted power-curve function; it is used to estimate turbine energy production and capacity factor.
empiricalModelParameters: P_{w,avg}: average wind-turbine power; P_w(v): turbine electrical power at wind speed v; f(v): wind-speed probability density

definition: A physical model that computes the power output of a wind turbine from wind speed, rotor area and power coefficient.
comment: Turbine power is the kinetic energy flux through the rotor multiplied by the power coefficient, used to estimate energy yield.
physicalModelParameters: P: turbine power ; ρ: air density ; A: rotor swept area ; Cp: power coefficient ; v: wind speed
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Kinetic energy flux of the wind

definition: The World-Wide Water Resources Assessment model (W3RA) is a global grid-based conceptual hydrological model simulating water storages and fluxes.
comment: It simulates soil moisture in several layers, vegetation, snow, surface water and groundwater storage; it is used for large-scale water-resource and runoff assessment including hydropower studies.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: Grid-based hydrological water-balance model representing multiple soil-moisture layers, vegetation, snow, surface water and groundwater storage.

definition: A hybrid model in which Weather Research and Forecasting model forecasts are corrected by a Kalman filter based on the clearness index.
comment: The Kalman filter removes systematic bias of the numerical weather prediction; it is used to improve solar irradiance forecasts.

definition: A configuration of the WRF-Solar numerical weather prediction model that assimilates MSG SEVIRI satellite radiances with three-dimensional variational data assimilation.
comment: Assimilated satellite observations improve the initial cloud and atmospheric state used to forecast surface solar irradiance; it is used for solar power forecasting.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: WRF-ARW Solar numerical weather prediction with three-dimensional variational assimilation of MSG/SEVIRI radiances.

definition: WRF with 3DVAR is the Weather Research and Forecasting model initialized through three-dimensional variational data assimilation of observations.
comment: 3DVAR combines background fields with observations by minimizing a cost function to improve initial conditions, which improves short-range wind and solar forecasts.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: WRF initialized/updated using three-dimensional variational data assimilation (3DVAR).

definition: A configuration of the Weather Research and Forecasting model initialised by four-dimensional variational data assimilation.
comment: 4DVAR adjusts the initial state so that model trajectories best fit observations over a time window, improving forecasts of wind, irradiance and other variables for renewable-energy applications.
physicalModelGoverningPrinciple: WRF initialized/updated using four-dimensional variational data assimilation (4DVAR).

definition: A hybrid forecasting model combining wavelet denoising, CEEMDAN decomposition and an outlier-robust extreme learning machine optimized by an improved atom search optimization.
comment: The series is denoised and decomposed into modes, each forecast by an ORELM whose parameters are tuned by IASO, for wind speed or power forecasting.

definition: A study-specific empirical model that estimates solar radiation from maximum and minimum temperature, rainfall and mean relative humidity.
comment: It was proposed for the Yucatán region and compared with other empirical solar-radiation models.
empiricalModelParameters: H: daily global solar radiation; H_0: extraterrestrial radiation; T_{\max},T_{\min}: daily maximum/minimum temperature; RH: mean relative humidity; RT_j: transformed rainfall term for day j; a,b,c,d: empirical coefficients
